name: Ownership Overhaul
author: Necrolesian
description: Assigns ownership to the many, many items and containers that rightly should be owned but weren't, and otherwise makes adjustments to item ownership.
usage_notes:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/OwTqf4W.png[/img]﻿[/center]
This mod assigns ownership to the many, many items and containers in Morrowind that rightly should be owned but weren't, and otherwise cleans up and adjusts item ownership.
 
Ownership in vanilla Morrowind is, in many cases, a mess. Lots and lots of stuff in people's houses or otherwise civilized areas, that certainly should be owned, is in fact unowned and therefore free for the taking, right from under the nose of the rightful owner. Masses of crates, barrels and other containers are sitting around in cities just waiting to be looted for free. Many guildhalls and other faction locations can be practically cleaned out by any newbie who signs up. Farmers will just stand there while you harvest all their crops right in front of them and then pretend like nothing happened. Nobody objects when you grab up all the lanterns and torches in town.
 
This mod aims to clean up this mess. The objective is to make owned everything that rightly should be owned, and unowned everything that shouldn't be.

[b]Details[/b]

I can't break down the changes made by this mod cell by cell (the plugin edits references in more than 600 cells), but the following describes this mod's changes in general terms:
 
- Containers in towns: Lots of unowned containers (crates and so on) were sitting around in cities free for the looting. This mod makes them all owned. In this respect it does basically the same thing as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47068]Container Ownership[/url] (or the other [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46886]Container Ownership[/url]), except that this mod makes owned outright many containers that Container Ownership makes faction owned.
 
- Light sources: Like containers, many light sources like lanterns and torches in cities and towns were unowned. Not anymore. No more free light sources for you. This works best with a good lighting overhaul, such as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47912]Let There Be Darkness[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47133]True Lights and Darkness[/url] or [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46291]Di.still.ed Lights[/url], that makes light sources actually useful.
 
- Guildhalls / faction owned stuff: Much faction owned stuff is now owned outright, while some has a higher rank requirement. Previously, much (if not most) of the content of many guildhalls was free for the taking if you're a member of the faction. Now for the most part only beds, supply chests, and a few other empty chests are faction owned at the lowest rank; a few other containers are faction owned with higher rank requirements, as is some clutter in common areas, while the other stuff in the guildhall is owned. This also applies to Ashlander camps, where previously lots of stuff outside was either faction owned or not owned at all.
 
- Farmers' fields: The crops in farmers' fields are now almost all owned. No longer can you clean out a farmer's entire crop right in front of him. The exception is for ingredients that the Imperial Cult specifically sends you to collect in their ingredient fetching quests (e.g. marshmerrow at Balur Salvu's farm). These plants are now faction owned by the Imperial Cult to ensure a cult member on the quests can harvest them.
 
- Doors: Lots of locked doors to/in people's houses or otherwise in civilized areas were unowned, meaning the rightful owner would stand there and watch you pick the lock without complaint. Now all these locked doors are owned. Previously owned but unlocked doors are now unowned, because there's no point in them being owned.
 
- Mines: Most stuff in mines that are actively being worked (i.e. those with friendly NPCs in them) is now owned. This was mainly an issue with eggmines, where all those kwama eggs were free for the taking. Ore rocks in actively worked mines were already owned, but those that were faction owned have been made owned outright, and other stuff in the mines (except wild plants) is also now owned. Mines without friendly NPCs have not been changed (everything is unowned).
 
- Keys: In many cases people's keys were sitting around in their houses and other areas unowned and free for the taking. There'll be no more of that kind of shenanigans.
 
- Gold: Most of the loose gold in civilized areas was unowned. Now you'll have to be sneaky about filling your pockets with it.
 
- House strongholds (e.g. Indarys Manor): Previously just about everything in the house strongholds was faction owned. Now all the stuff in people's houses (not the main buildings) is owned outright. In the main buildings, the stuff in the leader's/your room is faction owned, but stuff in other areas is owned outright. You might be in charge of the stronghold, but that doesn't mean you can just waltz in and swipe your subordinates' personal stuff.
 
- Vampire headquarters (e.g. Galom Daeus): These aren't regular dungeons, and while you might be here on (relatively) friendly terms, that doesn't mean you should be able to grab everything in sight with no consequence. Just about everything in these locations that wasn't already owned is now owned by the clan's leader. Given the contempt the leaders have for you, I don't think they'd appreciate you partially cleaning out their headquarters.
 
- Tel Fyr: The good stuff in Tel Fyr and the Corprusarium is now owned. Divayth Fyr practically dares you to try to rip him off, but that doesn't mean he won't react negatively if he catches you at it. (The two newly owned containers in Fyr's office are vulnerable to telekinesis from the hall outside, but the key on his table is more of a challenge.)

- Ahnassi's House: The stuff in Ahnassi's house in Pelagiad should rightly be owned by her, but male characters can get invited to share her home as part of her quest, at which point it should be okay to take the stuff and sleep in her bed. This has been solved by assigning this stuff a global variable, similar to how beds for rent at inns work - you'll be permitted to take her stuff once you've been invited into her home.
 
- Dungeons: Dungeons are almost entirely untouched; in almost all cases nothing is owned. A couple very rare exceptions have been made for stuff rightly belonging to friendly NPCs in otherwise unfriendly locations (e.g. some of the stuff in Ald Daedroth Antechamber).
 
- Outcast Ashlander yurts: Most of the stuff in outcast Ashlander yurts with hostile NPCs was owned. Now this stuff is unowned. The same is true of the Velothi tower Shara, a dungeon with only hostiles.
 
- Stuff that really needs to be unowned: There are some items that, for various reasons, need to remain unowned. This is mostly stuff that a quest (for an honorable faction or otherwise not a stealy kind of quest) requires or invites you to take. Examples include Gambolpuddy in Ald Daedroth and Drinar Varyon's Dwemer tube, among others.
 
- Owned activators: In some cases activators other than beds were uselessly owned. For example, just about every furn_de_bar object in the game was owned. The waterfalls in Vivec's canalworks areas and the chimes in Ashlander wise women's yurts are other examples. This stuff is no longer owned.
[b]
Installation[/b]

Use a mod management tool such as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45439]Wrye Mash[/url], or just copy the plugin to your Data Files directory and select it in the Morrowind Launcher.

Use either the .esm  version or the .esp version, but not both. If you're not sure which version to use, the .esm version is safer in terms of compatibility.
 
The .esm version should load after [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45096]Patch for Purists[/url] but before any other .esm mods. The .esp version should be relatively early in your load order, before any other mods that touch the affected objects, unless you know what you're doing.

[b]Requirements[/b]

This mod requires both Tribunal and Bloodmoon.

[b]Compatibility[/b]

For the most part, this plugin edits only cell references, so mods that don't touch cell references will mostly be fully compatible. There is one exception: the mod edits one of Ahnassi's "share a care" dialogue entries to set a global variable needed to permit the player to take her stuff afterward. If you're using another mod that changes this particular dialogue entry, you might find yourself unable to legally take her stuff when you should be able to, without a patch.
 
There might also be compatibility issues with mods that change cell references (e.g. moving stuff around, or removing references and replacing them with new ones). I recommend putting this mod early in your load order.

If you're using any .esm mods that touch the affected objects (in particular some of RandomPal's [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48807]town[/url] [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48689]overhauls[/url]), you'll want to use the .esm version of this mod. Load it after Patch for Purists but before your other .esms.

If you use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47305]Morrowind Anti-Cheese[/url], I recommend using the OO-compatible version available [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/49232]here[/url] instead. Alternatively, if you're also using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47129]BTB's Game Improvements[/url], use the BTBGI-compatible version of Anti-Cheese [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/50308]here[/url].

There should be no conflict with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45096]Patch for Purists[/url]. This mod was created with PFP loaded, then the dependency on PFP was removed afterward, so any PFP fixes to the affected objects (e.g. adjusting position) are incorporated.
 
There is a very minor conflict with any version of [url=http://mw.modhistory.com/download-56-12938]Diverse Ore Veins[/url] / [url=http://mw.modhistory.com/download-56-13484]CorrectUV Ore Replacer[/url], including the version of that plugin packaged along with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46599]Graphic Herbalism[/url]. That mod deletes the cell references to ore rocks and replaces them with new references to new containers, and the new references are not modified by my mod.
 
This means that if you're using that mod, you won't see my mod's changes to ore rock ownership (regardless of load order). This isn't actually that big a deal. Ore rocks in mines with friendly NPCs are already owned in vanilla Morrowind; my mod only makes some of them owned outright rather than faction owned. In fact, this affects only one cell: Sudanit Mine. And it can only be taken advantage of by the Archmaster of House Redoran. So I definitely still recommend using both mods together.

[b]Contact[/b]

Feel free to contact me on the Nexus with any comments or suggestions. You can also find me on Discord as Necrolesian#9692.

[b]Usage[/b]

You can use this however you want.

name: Arrive Whenever - Start Time and Timescale for OpenMW
author: Leaposter
description: Configurable arrival time and timescale when starting a new game.
usage_notes:
[b]Description:[/b]
You've heard of "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51567]Arrive At Night[/url]" and "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59179]Arrive Before Dawn[/url]", now get ready for "[b]Arrive Whenever[/b]"!
This mod allows for either randomized or user-configurable arrival time when starting a new game.

The timescale for a new game can also be configured. For reference, when configuring the timescale:
Morrowind default is 30, Skyrim default is 20, real time is 1.

[b]Features & Functionality:[/b]
[list]
[*]All settings apply exactly once, when starting a new game. The timescale setting will persist so long it isn't changed later by another mod or by console command.[/*]
[*]Optionally Randomize your arrival time when starting a new game (Default).[/*]
[*]Optionally limit randomization to Dawn, Day, Dusk, and Night.[/*]
[*]Optionally disable randomization in settings, and instead, select an exact offset for your arrival time when starting a new game.[/*]
[*]Optionally adjust the timescale when starting a new game.[/*]
[*]Settings can be configured from the settings menu on the title screen, before starting a new game.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Requirements:[/b]
[list]
[*]OpenMW 0.51 or later.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Compatibility:[/b]
[list]
[*]The time change is all handled in Lua, and only runs once when starting a new game. This should be compatible with all alternate start mods.[/*]
[*]If you were previously using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46332]Timescale Change[/url], it can be uninstalled, as Arrive Whenever now replaces its functionality. Having both installed won't break anything, but Arrive Whenever's timescale choice will take precedence if it's enabled. [/*]
[*]Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52462]Dynamic Timescale[/url] as of v0.3.[/*]
[*]Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57526]Sun's Dusk[/url] as of v0.5[/*]
[/list]

name: Expansion Delay
author: Half11
description: This mod fixes Bethesda's overly enthusiastic expansion hooks by delaying the Dark Brotherhood attacks (for Tribunal) and limiting intrustive dialogue topics to a few NPCs (Bloodmoon).
usage_notes:
[size=3][img]data:image/png;base64,[/img]
<br />
<br />This mod fixes Bethesda's overly enthusiastic expansion hooks by delaying the Dark Brotherhood attacks (for Tribunal) and limiting intrustive dialogue topics to a few NPCs (Bloodmoon). Bethesda probably assumed that everyone would be high enough level when the expansions came out and didn't bother to account for new players and characters. 
<br />
<br />[i]Note: You might know a similair mod by me called Better Expansion Implementations. I got feedback that such an essential mod should not be burried in my Misc Mods page, so I have decided to give the mod its own page, a name that is easier to remember and updated some dialogue filters.[/i]
<br />
<br />
<br />Tribunal:
<br />[/size][list]
<br />[*][size=3]You won't be bothered by assassins until pretty far into the main quest. [color=#ff7700]*SPOILER ALERT*[/color] You won't be attacked until you have been named Hlaalu Hortator. An early assassin attack doesn't make sense lore-wise. Almalexia straight up calls the PC Nerevarine. Also, Helseth wouldn't plan an assassination on a no-name. [color=#ff7700]*END OF SPOILER*[/color][/size]
<br />[*][size=3]The expansion forces you to start the Tribunal quest, to be no longer bothered by assassins when you rest. To prevent this forced feeling I made the stream of assassins stop earlier, at the time a guard tells you the assassins are likely members of the Dark Brotherhood ("A guard has told me that my attackers were likely members of the Dark Brotherhood, and that I have been targeted for assassination. He suggests I speak with Apelles Matius in Ebonheart for more information."). At that point (TR_dbAttack 30) you have all the information you need, and the possibility to start the Tribunal questline has been introduced in a not too compelling way. You no longer have to interrupt your adventures for a trip to Ebonheart to stop the attacks. Lorewise the Dark Brotherhood attacks should start during a certain point in the Vvardenfell mainquest. It would be awkward to be forced to start the Tribunal mainquest at this point. [/size]
<br />[*][color=#ff7700][size=3]*SPOILER ALERT*[/size][/color][size=3] A check was added if you killed Dagoth Ur, in case you do the main quest the backdoor way, and are never named Nerevarine by any Ashlander tribe. [color=#ff7700]*END OF SPOILER*[/color][/size]
<br />[*][size=3]Farming the assassins is still possible (if that's your thing). Just don't talk about the attacks to guards.[/size]
<br />[/list][size=3]
<br />Bloodmoon:
<br />[/size][list]
<br />[*][size=3]You won't be bothered by the dialogue that Bloodmoon introduces until level 6 (just like Bethesda did with Tribunal expansion on the Xbox). This was necessary to prevent the new dialogue from blocking other dialogue at low levels.[/size]
<br />[*][size=3]Now only one random generic Imperial guard has his son send to Solstheim. I found it hard to believe that Jonus Maximus, being a high ranking legionary, had no idea why his son was sent to Solstheim in Illy's Solsteim Rumour Fix.[/size]
<br />[*][size=3]What I have taken over from Illy is binding the other rumour ("I heard there...north of Vvardenfell.") to the Agent class. This was done to prevent every NPC from having the Solstheim topic.[/size]
<br />[*][size=3]If the player somehow missed the second quest update (BM_Rumors 50) after hearing about Solstheim for the first time (BM_Rumors 10), Scouts can also update your journal ("That's the frozen...transportation in Khuul."). The permanent topic about getting to Solstheim is also tied to the Scout class now ("A terrible place...any reason to go.").[/size]
<br />[*][size=3]Fixed dialogue filtering, so that NPC's that aren't supposed to have no dialogue topics at all (NoLore), won't have topics in their dialogue box.[/size]
<br />[*][size=3]Now you'll actually have a chance to see the Dunmer rumour ("I've been told ...is beyond me.") regarding Solstheim on Vvardenfell. Previously it was highly unlikely to come across this rumour.[/size]
<br />[size=3][/size][*][color=#ff7700][size=3]*SPOILER ALERT*[/size][/color][size=3] Louis Beauchamp (NPC outside Ald'ruhn Mages Guild) will be disabled until you started the Bloodmoon main quest. This was done to prevent new players from getting spoiled by his quest, sending them to Solstheim.[color=#ff7700] *END OF SPOILER*[/color][/size]

description: Restricts Solstheim dialogue options and rumors. Now only Jonus Maximus, NPCs who are Agents, and the people of Solstheim and Khuul will talk about Solstheim. Unique dialogue added for Nords.
usage_notes:
A few years ago Illy released a [url=http://mw.modhistory.com/download-21-13960]mod[/url]﻿ which restricted the topic Solstheim and the latest rumors associated with Solstheim to a handful of NPCs, and later [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/60629711]nomoresam[/url] released a [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46208?tab=description]fix[/url]﻿ for it. Since according to the description of these mods they can be modified and used freely, I made this improvement, which aims to fine-tune them even more.

[b]What did their mod do?

[/b]- The only Imperial Legionnaire now whose son was stationed at Fort Frostmoth is Jonus Maximus
- Besides him only S'Virr, agents and residents of Khuul know about the place, so nobody else talked about "Solstheim" and the "latest rumors" associted with the place

[b]What is my contribution to the mod?

[/b]- It adds unique dialogue to Nords who are also residents of Khuul or belong to the agent class. There are four nords in Khuul, and several Nords who are also agents. I think that it wouldn't make sense for them to call Solstheim "a terrible place," especially because in [b]vanilla [/b]dialogue, Solstheim Nords tell you that this place is nothing compared to Skyrim. Expect TES V: Skyrim terminology, in which they call everyone who considers Solstheim to be harsh a "milk drinker," or claim that Solstheim is a place for true men to prove their mettle.

[b]Does this mod require the mod made by Illy and nomoresam?

usage_notes:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/wgqxwAU.png[/img]﻿[/center]

Think it's odd that there's a legal assassination practice in Morrowind, yet no matter how much trouble the player causes, there's never a writ for the player? If so, you're on the right mod page.

Features:
-If the player meets certain conditions, they will be assaulted by the Morag Tong in the same manner as Tribunal's Dark Brotherhood.
-Like the Dark Brotherhood, there are 5 ranks of assassins that are based on player level.
-There are multiple NPCs with leveled items for each rank, so there will be some variety in the attacks.
-Support for various mods to make the assassins use gear from said mods

[*]If you are a high-enough level to fight the level 20 or level 30 Morag Tong assassins, you may be attacked by more than one.[/*]
[*]If you are rank 8 or 9 of the Morag Tong, you will never be assaulted.[/*]
[*]Mournhold, Sotha Sil, and a few other plot-sensible locations are safe from Morag Tong attacks.[/*]
[*]If you clear your bounty, you will no longer be assaulted.[/*]
[*]If you complete a quest for a great house in a manner that would upset another great house, the Morag Tong will come after you once per quest.[/*]
[*]The Morag Tong only operate within Morrowind, so Solstheim and Cyrodiil are safe.[/*]

name: Greetings for No Lore
author: Caeris
description: Replaces the three standard No Lore greetings with over sixty new ones.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Introduction[/b][/size][size=3]

There is only three greetings for NPCs marked "No Lore" in vanilla Morrowind. This can become very repetitive for the player, especially if they are playing quest mods. This mod simply replaces those three greetings with over sixty new ones.

The new greetings take into account:

- Disposition
- Race (Khajiit vs non-Khajiit) 
- & how many times you have spoken to the NPC

[/size][size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size][size=3]

This mod includes a patch for LGNPC.

This mod should be compatible with most other dialogue mods as all dialogue is added to Greeting 9 in the dialogue window.

[/size][size=4][b]Load Order[/b][/size][size=3]
 
Please note that this mod contains optional patches for other mods, so it's important that you follow my standard rules below.

1. Another Mod.esp
2. This Mod.esp
3. Patch for Both Mods.esp
4. Merged Objects.esp

You can safely assume any mods I author follow the above standard rules unless otherwise specified.

This mod is included in [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55615]Morrowind Extended Cut[/url]﻿.

[center][b]I  hope you enjoy this nifty little mod,
- Caeris.[/b][/center][/size]

name: Djangos Dialogue 1.4
author: Von Djangos
description:
Hundreds of new lines of text dialogue for all NPCs, which helps to remedy the repetition and dialogue fatigue that came with the original game.
The 1.4 update is mostly around greetings - new greetings by class, new greetings about your outfit and reputation, and fully filtered dialogue for weather
and time of day
usage_notes:
[b]What's in the mod?[/b]

Hundreds of new lines of text dialogue for all NPCs, which helps to remedy the repetition and dialogue fatigue that came with the original game.

[b]The 1.4 update[/b] is mostly around greetings - new greetings by class, new greetings about your outfit and reputation, and fully filtered dialogue for weather
and time of day for all shipmasters, caravaneers and publicans.

If you haven't played with the mod before, this also adds...

[b]Background:[/b]
Hundreds of new backgrounds, filtered by class, and then by race within those classes. Great Houses also have unique backgrounds for their most popular classes - Redoran Warriors, for instance, or Telvanni sorcerers. These have been expanded in 1.4.
[b]
Little secret:[/b]
Over 100 new secrets - some are faction specific, and some are class specific. There are many Dark Elf specific secrets too. These have been expanded in 1.4.

[b]Little advice:[/b]
Adds about 50 new little advice lines. 1.4 adds specific advice for the Telvanni and Hlaalu, as well as specific advice for commoners so they're not waxing
lyrical about casting spells or fighting monsters.

[b]Services & Someone in Particular:[/b]
Originally the 'services' topic simply had one response per city, regardless of where you where. This was pretty immersion breaking. 
Now Npcs will respond according to where they are, giving a better sense of place and making the game less robotic. 

[b]And more:[/b]
Lots of little tidbits hidden around the game. You can ask the Telvanni and Redoran about other Houses now, or see custom persuasion responses for certain quests. Some small villages have more variety in their rumours.

Cleaned with tesame.

Enjoy the mod!

[b]History:
[/b]1.44 - Added more variety to how NPCs respond to you having a high bounty. 
1.43 - Added a series of new 'Little Secrets' that point you towards major and master trainers not mentioned in dialogue
1.42 - A host of spelling fixes courtesy of Danae.
1.41 - Rumours -> Rumors, tweaks to publican and caravaneer greetings, more backgrounds, tweaked text for 'service' classes. Telvanni topic for Redoran updated.
1.4 - Custom greetings, filtered by class, time of day, weather and more
1.3 - More backgrounds, this time for key classes of the Great Dunmer Houses
1.2 - Added another 100 entries to the 'background' topic
1.1 - Added over 300 new entries for the 'background' topic - split by class, race and gender
1.0 - Initial release, superceeds my old 'little secrets' and 'good service' mods

name: Djangos Dialogue - Tamriel Rebuilt patch
author: Jonado
description: Patch to incorporate some of Djangos Dialogue into Tamriel Rebuilt.
usage_notes:
With the 22.11 update of Tamriel Rebuilt and version 9 of Tamriel Data, new dialogue filters have been added to prevent most of the general dialogue (more specifically, dialogue with NoLore filters) from the base game to appear on the mainland. The reason for doing so was that some of the dialogue is too Vvardenfell centric. Thanks to the tremendous effort of two Tamriel Rebuilt members, all dialogue that makes sense to appear on the Mainland - and sometimes in the other provinces - were instead copied into TR_Mainland or Tamriel_Data with the new filters. However, a drawback is that general dialogue from other mods will not appear on the Mainland, either.

One such mod is Djangos Dialogue, which enriches the Vanilla dialogue, and adds a lot of dialogue that makes sense on the mainland as well (and quite a lot that doesn't). This mod copies the relevant dialogue and applies the new filters to it. Some of it will also appear in the other provinces (i.e. Skyrim - Home of the Nords and Province Cyrodiil), but in my opinion not enough to motivate a standalone patch. I have tried to preserve the original dialogue lines as far as possible, but sometimes slight modfications were necessary to fit the new setting.

Acknowledgements: I would like to thank [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/40926435]Von Djangos[/url] for writing the original dialogue and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/77253]Alvazir[/url] for fixing various bugs with the original mod. I would also like to thank [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/881270]Evil Eye[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/38286905]Rakanishu[/url] from the TR team for their work with the new NoLore system, and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/64030]Greatness7[/url] for the [b]tes3conv[/b] tool.

[u][b][size=4]Description[/size][/b][/u]

[size=3]In the vanilla game, you were supposed to have to purchase "Hospitality Papers" before being able to get services in Sadrith Mora. Dialogue suggested this, and the papers were available to buy, but the mechanic of service refusal was never actually implemented. quorn made a great straight forward plugin to fix this: [/size]

[size=3][url=http://mw.modhistory.com/download-90-6206]http://mw.modhistory.com/download-90-6206[/url][/size]

[size=3]I felt that more could be added to implement this more fully so I expanded on quorn's work.

This plugin contains everything that the original did and more.

Thank you quorn for this mod, it brought my attention to this issue. And thank you for being so generous with your permissions, so that I was able to make this. (If anyone has a contact for quorn so I can thank him more directly, that would be great)
[/size]

[b][size=4][u]What's New?
[/u][/size]
[/b][size=3]- When you get service refusal and are told you need papers, you can now ask what they are and where to get them by inquiring about the topics "Hospitality Papers" and "Gateway"[/size]

[size=3]- According to vanilla dialogue you need Hospitality Papers unless you are kin of house Telvanni or have achieved the rank of Retainer or higher. Just joining house Telvanni will no longer cut it.[/size]

[size=3]- New audio and text dialogue for guards, harassing you about having Papers. Includes newly recorded lines from original Morrowind voice actor [url=https://jeffbakervo.com/]Jeff Baker[/url]

[/size][size=3]- An increased unfriendliness from Sadrith Mora guards in general, lowered disposition and hostile audio and text lines, make Sadrith Mora feel truly unwelcoming and xenophobic to outlanders and newcomers, especially non-dunmer, and outright racist if you're an Argonian or Khajiit

[/size][size=3]- Edited the text of the Papers themselves so that they actually make sense, for example, the original Papers said (paraphrasing for concision):  with these papers you can conduct your business freely, provided that you do not well and truly observe the law.
[/size][size=3]Now they say (paraphrasing for concision): with these papers you can conduct your business freely, provided that you do not fail to well and truly observe the law.

- Following on from that last point, if you get caught breaking the law in town, your papers will now be taken away[/size]

[size=3]- The papers now cost 50 gold instead of 25, hopefully nowhere near enough to actually inconvenience the player massively or make the game too frustrating, but enough that you might grumble "50 gold?!?..." [/size]

[size=3]- There is also now a penalty for losing them or having them confiscated (you will have to pay a lot more for a new copy)[/size]

[size=3]- Relevant dialogue is added and tweaked to help you find your way around (providing the NPCs like you enough) as a first time player or someone role-playing being fresh off the boat. New dialogue for the Prefect of Hospitality as well. [/size]

[size=3]- A unique texture and icon for the Hospitality Papers themselves[/size]

[size=3]+ A bonus mod that better filters guard's dialogue so that non-Imperial guards have slightly more unique greetings and responses to the topic of "Imperial Law". Also, guards will no longer play the audio line "Need I call the guards?" when they don't like you.

[u][b][size=3]Grazelands[/size][/b][/u]

[list]
[*]The Grazelands are described as both arid and as having regular rainfall. See Item C-003 [url=http://www.theassimilationlab.com/forums/topic/16025-uniformity-mods-for-mw-gameplay-vs-text/]here[/url]. Grazelands have a 10% chance of rain, whereas the Ascadian Isles only have a 5% chance. So, gameplay suggests that developers went with the regular rainfall concept.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Vvardenfell and Geography of Vvardenfell
[/i]
[color=#ea9999][size=3]Except for the settled southwest, Vvardenfell is covered by hostile desert wastes, arid grasslands, and volcanic badlands, and thinly populated by the nomadic Ashlander tribes.[/size][/color][size=3] 
[/size][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]Except for the settled southwest and the Grazelands of the northeast, Vvardenfell is mostly covered by hostile wastes and volcanic badlands, and thinly populated by the nomadic Ashlander tribes.[/color]
[/size]
[i]Topic: The Dark Elven Curse[/i]

[size=3][color=#ea9999]In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derives from 'the Dark Elven Curse,' which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the northeastern wastelands, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in the Dunmer's own accounts of their past.[/color]
[/size][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derives from 'the Dark Elven Curse', which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the ash wastes, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in the Dunmer's own accounts of their past.
[/color][/size]
[list]
[*]The Grazelands are also said to have NO roads or tracks, there are obviously some tracks through the Grazelands.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Grazelands [/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]There are no roads or tracks in the Grazelands, but travel is easy across the rolling plains.
[/size][/color][color=#b6d7a8][size=3]There are no paved roads in the Grazelands, but travel is easy across the tracks and rolling plains.
[/size][/color]
[list]
[*]Tel Fyr is described as being in the Grazelands. It is nowhere near the Grazelands.
[/list]
[i]Topic: Grazelands[/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]Permanent settlements in the Grazelands include Vos village and the towers of Tel Vos and Tel Fyr.
[/size][/color][size=3][color=#b6d7a8]Permanent settlements in the Grazelands include Vos village and the tower of Tel Vos.

[/color][/size][b][u][size=3]Coastguard Cutters

[/size][/u][/b]NPCs will tell you that there are Coastguard cutters docked at Seyda Neen who control smuggling along the coast. There are two problems with this, firstly there are no Coastguard cutters present in game, docked at Seyda Neen or otherwise. Secondly, NPCs who are not in Seyda Neen will refer to the cutters being docked "here" when asked about Seyda Neen, rather than "there".

I do not consider it inconsistent to reference something that the player can't encounter in-game, on the contrary I think this can help with world building. But when it is explicitly stated that something can be found in a location here and now, when it can't, just seems confusing. As such, this is my fix:

[i]Topic: Seyda Neen (Filtered for Gnaar Mok)[/i]

[color=#ea9999][size=3]The Coastguard cutters of Census and Excise docked here control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.[/size][/color]
[color=#b6d7a8][size=3]The Coastguard cutters of Census and Excise who dock there control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.

[/size][/color]Other responses to the Seyda Neen topic are edited accordingly.

[size=3][b][u]Herd Animals
[/u][/b][/size]
When inquiring about herd animals you will be told:

[color=#ea9999][size=3]The two most common herd animals of the Ashlanders are the guar and the shalk. The guar is a large biped, trained as a beast of burden, and raised for meat and hides. Wild guard are encountered in the wilderness; they're usually quite peaceful. The shalk is a large, unaggressive beetle, raised for meat and resin from its shells.

[/size][/color]It is mentioned that wild guar are usually quite peaceful and that shalk are unaggressive. In game both of these animals are aggressive. I have checked every book and piece of dialogue containing the word "guar" and containing the word "shalk". I cannot find any reference to guars being anything other than peaceful. I did, however, find references to shalks being aggressive. This, couple with the fact that we do meet docile guars in game, lead me to fix these two inconsistencies by making wild guar peaceful, as described, and updating the line like so: 

[size=3][color=#b6d7a8]The two most common herd animals of the Ashlanders are the guar and the shalk. The guar is a large biped, trained as a beast of burden, and raised for meat and hides. Wild guars are encountered in the wilderness; they're usually quite peaceful. The shalk is a large beetle, raised for meat and resin from its shells.[/color]

[b][u][size=3]Temple Attributes[/size][/u][/b]

The Tribunal Temple faction's favored attributes are Personality and Intelligence and yet it is inferred in the book "Fellowship of the Temple" that their favored attributes are Personality and Willpower.

[color=#ea9999][size=3]Those who follow the Tribunal must have the Personality to lead others and the Willpower to resist the world's temptations.[/size][/color]
[color=#b6d7a8][size=3]Those who follow the Tribunal must have the personality to lead others and the will and cunning to resist the world's temptations.[/size][/color]

This leaves it compatible with any mods that might correct this inconsistency by changing the Temple's favored attribute.

[/size][u][b][size=3]Ajira[/size][/b][/u]

[list]
[*][size=3]Ajira sends you on a mages guild quest to find, among other things, four samples of heather and willow anther. [/size]
[/list][i]
"Yes, Ajira must study flowers now. Ajira needs samples of Gold Kanet, Stoneflower Petals, Willow Anther, and Heather. These can all be found on the shores of Lake Amaya." 

[/i]Ajira has 5 restocking copies of Willow Anther and Heather that you can buy from her, and she will accept the ones you've bought from her for the quest. 

This mod simply removes those flowers from her inventory so she can no longer sell them to you. 

Thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/4709296?tab=user+files]Gavrilo98[/url] for reporting this inconsistency. If anyone is interested in a stand-alone fix for this, with a re-balancing twist, check out his mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47585]here[/url].

[list]
[*][size=3]Galbedir and Ajira have bet who first advance to journeyman rank however Galbedir already has journeyman rank. Also worth noting is that Ajira has rank of associate.[/size]
[/list]
In v1.1 I changed both character's rank to Apprentice, 1 below Journeyman. Thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/2104994]zelazko[/url] for the suggestion.

[b][u][size=3]Gravedust[/size][/u][/b]

[url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Gravedust]Gravedust[/url] is described as a "spirit-affinitive dust taken from remains buried in consecrated ground." Gravedust cannot be taken from remains and is only found very rarely on consecrated ground. So I made it find-able in burial urns that would usually only contain bonemeal. Now there is a 50% chance to find bonemeal and a 50% chance to find gravedust.

Please note, this change is not included with the main file and is it's own plugin in a separate download here.

[b]Installation[/b]
[size=3][left]Get it in your Data Files folder, activate it in your launcher, and keep it fairly high up the load order so other things can overwrite it if they need to. I've re-dated it so it should be fairly high up by default for vanilla engine users. If you use Patch for Purists make sure FMI_Misc loads after it, which again, it will by default in the vanilla engine.[/left][/size][center][u]Other Mods in the Finished Morrowind - Inconsistencies Series[/u]

name: FMI - Service Refusal and Contraband
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Fixes lore to gameplay inconsistencies pertaining to contraband items and service refusal.
usage_notes:
[left][size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link: 
[/b][/size][size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695 [/url]**[/b][/size]

This module of my ongoing inconsistencies project aims to fix all inconsistencies between the lore and what is, or more often [i]isn't, [/i]present in-game pertaining to contraband, infectious or illegal items and anything to do with service refusal, excluding Sadrith Mora Hospitality Papers which are covered [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46107]here[/url].[/left][center][size=6]
[b][color=#ffe599]Vanilla Quotes[/color][color=#fff2cc]﻿[/color][/b][/size][/center]
[i][center]Relating to Dwemer Artifacts[/center][/i][center][i]"Weapons, armor, housewares, coins, and other items of Dwemer design are often found in Dwemer ruins. They are prized by historians and antiquarians, and very valuable. The Emperor, however, has declared all newly discovered Dwemer artifacts to be possessions of the Crown, and forbids their trade or sale. Now smuggling Dwemer artifacts is treason, but smugglers will still risk execution for such a profitable crime."[/i][/center][i]

[/i]
[i][center]Relating to Raw Glass[/center][/i][i][center]"Smuggling raw glass is a crime. All raw glass belongs to the Emperor, so it's the crime of treason, and punished by death. But... there's so much money to be made selling black market raw glass that it's a rare merchant who'll refuse to buy a piece from you. Of course, if the mine guards catch you stealing raw glass, they just kill you. Which is why we don't steal raw glass."[/center]
[/i]

[i][center]Relating to Raw Ebony[/center][/i][i]"Smuggling ebony is a crime. All ebony belongs to the Emperor, so it's the crime of treason, and punished by death. But... there's so much money to be made selling black market ebony that it's a rare merchant who'll refuse to buy a piece from you. Of course, if the mine guards catch you stealing ebony, they just kill you. Which is why we don't steal ebony."
[/i]
[i]
[/i][center][i]Relating to Imperial Charter[/i][/center][left][/left][i]"I am Cunius Pelelius, a principal and charter-holder of the Caldera Mining Company. I cannot imagine why someone like you should think you have business with me, but I will listen, if you can be brief and polite."[/i]

[i]"I'm keeping an eye on the Caldera Mining Company. We all think something fishy is going on -- probably several somethings -- but we haven't penetrated their operation. They're probably skimming cash, or raw ebony, or both. But we're not quite sure who 'they' are. The Company has tight security. Worried about the Redoran -- who think THEY should own Caldera -- and the Twin Lamps, who want to embarrass the Company or help slaves escape."[/i]

[i]"I'll tell you why Cunius Pelelius is slow to redeem his pledged donation. Because he's gotten in a bit of money trouble. And he's solving the problem by skimming from the mine and smuggling raw ebony. That's what people say in private, anyway. It would be hard to get proof. The slaves in the Caldera ebony mines would know. But they would be hard to persuade to talk. They're afraid, and who can blame them?"[/i]

[i]"He takes raw ebony from the mines. He does not tell anyone. He pays no tax on it. He steals it from the mine, and avoids the tax. So when he sells it to smugglers, he makes a very fine profit indeed. No costs. All profit."[/i]


[i][center]General[/center][/i][left][/left][i]"The East Empire Company is a monopolistic mercantile enterprise chartered by the Emperor and managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor. The Company has sole authority to trade in certain goods, like flin, raw ebony, raw glass, and Dwemer artifacts, and it also enjoys favorable tariffs and regulations for import and export of other common and exotic goods, like kwama eggs, marshmerrow pulp, saltrice, and Telvanni bug musk."

"The Fighters Guild is chartered by the Empire. Citizens can hire us to take care of pests and handle the tasks the Legion doesn't want to dirty its hands with[/i]."



[b][size=6][color=#ffe599][center]What This Mod Does - The Basics[/center]
[/color][/size][/b][list]
[*]In accordance with in-game dialogue, it will be a rare merchant who refuses to trade in raw glass, raw ebony or Dwermer artifacts. 
[/list][color=#b6b6b6]Here is what constitutes a Dwemer artifact in this mod (highest to lowest value):

Misc_dwrv_artifact50 : Dwemer Coherer
Misc_dwrv_coin00 : Dwemer Coin
Misc_dwrv_pitcher00 : Ornate Dwemer Pitcher
Misc_dwrv_artifact60 : Dwemer Tube
misc_dwrv_artifact00 : Dwemer Cylinder
Misc_dwrv_goblet10 : Ornate Dwemer Goblet
Misc_dwrv_goblet00 : Ornate Dwemer Goblet
Misc_dwrv_mug00 : Dwemer Mug
Misc_dwrv_bowl00 : Ornate Dwemer Bowl

Note that Dwemer papers that are essential to quests are not included.[/color]

[list]
[*][size=3]Empire-affiliated NPCs will take the law more seriously and Imperial Legion traders will take an especially dim view of those seen as trying to peddle contraband. You may be asked to hand over the items or else be accused of smuggling and thus treason.[/size]
[/list]
[color=#b6b6b6]However, even Legion NPCs will turn something of a blind eye to Dwemer weapons and armor, in the sense that they will never threaten to charge you with treason or ask you to hand in the items. They will simply refuse you service. This is because many NPCs in-game carry Dwemer armor and weapons so it can be assumed that “personal use” of weapons and armor not “newly discovered” is not prohibited. I also felt that from a gameplay perspective having to turn over all your Dwemer weapons and armor or receive a death warrant was too restrictive.

Also, Legion NPCs will be more peaceable if you are a member of the East Empire Company or Legion, with the player simply handing over all of the type of contraband in question as opposed to being shaken down for all contraband items. 
[/color]
[list]
[*][size=3]I decided not to add the ability for the player to acquire an Imperial Charter. [/size]
[/list][size=3]
[/size][color=#b6b6b6]The fact that Cunius Pelelius is still breaking the law by selling raw ebony outside of the proper channels despite having an Imperial Charter, made me feel that there would be no point in allowing the player to acquire one.[/color]

[list]
[*][size=3]In accordance with in-game dialogue, stealing from raw glass or ebony mines will now be an instant death sentence.[/size]
[/list][size=3]
[/size][b][size=6][color=#ffe599]
[center]What This Mod Does - Further Breakdown[/center][/color][/size][/b]
Let’s look at who will refuse service for contraband and how that will play out.

Note that I have filtered service refusal lines by class to reduce the chance of service refusal for services where bartering goods is not an option. As such, several factions have service refusal lines despite not having any NPCs in the vanilla game that would refuse you service. I did this for the sake of mod compatibility.


[b][u]Fighters Guild[/u] 
[/b]
As the Fighters Guild is chartered by the Empire, and Fighters Guild members guard Vvardenfell’s East Empire Company store rooms, I felt that members of the FG would be less than inclined to buy and sell contraband.

The Fighters Guild will turn a blind eye towards Dwarven weapons and armor.

There are no vanilla NPCs in this faction who would refuse you service for contraband.

[b]“The Fighters Guild is chartered by the Emperor and has a responsibility to protect commerce. So don’t even think about asking me if I want to buy that raw ebony.”
[/b][b]

[/b][center][b]“The Fighters Guild is chartered by the Emperor. Part of our responsibility is to protect commerce. It wouldn’t look very good if we went around trading Dwemer artifacts now would it? Please put that down before we trade.”[/b][/center]

[u][left][b]Imperial Knights[/b][/left][/u]
While this faction does not feature at all in vanilla Morrowind, I added service refusal lines for compatibility with other mods.

Imperial Knights will turn a blind eye to Dwemer weapons and armor.


[center][b]“I will do no dealings with one who carries the Emperor’s precious raw glass.”[/b][/center]

[u][b]Census & Excise Office[/b]
[/u]
Refuses service for raw ebony, raw glass, Dwemer artifacts, weapons and armor. Appropriate dialogue changes exist for if the player is a member of the East Empire Trading Company.

There are no vanilla NPCs in this faction who would refuse you service for contraband.
[center]
Player is a member of the EEC:

[b]“As I’m sure you’re aware, I can do no dealings in raw ebony. You’ll have to take that to the Company.”[/b]

If the player is not a member of the EEC:

[b]“I cannot do business with anyone who carries raw ebony. It belongs to the Emperor and should be handed in to the East Empire Company.”[/b]

If the player carries Dwemer weapons or armor:

[b]“The Emperor has declared all newly discovered Dwarven artifacts to be possessions of the Crown, which forbids their trade or sale. You must set down any Dwemer weapons, including that one, before we trade.”[/b][b]
[/b][/center]

[u][b]Imperial Cult[/b][/u]

Much the same as Census & Excise but there are several vanilla Imperial Cult NPCs who will refuse you service for contraband.

[u][b]Imperial Legion[/b][/u]

If you are a member of the Legion or East Empire Company, then service refusal will be much the same as with the above mentioned factions, with the line taking into account the player’s rank. However, if you are not a member of either faction, then you will be given a choice, to hand in the contraband or face the penalty for treason.

[left]Publicans in the Legion will still simply refuse you service.

In version 1.0, you could not cheat the lore by dropping your goods in plain sight and picking them up again after you’ve finished bartering, unless you were very stealthy. I removed this feature in 1.5 because I felt that it was something that could be done better with the use of Lua script. I may have a look at this again once OpenMW gets Lua scripting capabilities.
[b]
[/b][/left][center][b]“Dwemer coins are the property of the Emperor and must be delivered to the East Empire Company. Hand them in now along with any other contraband goods. Refusal will be seen as a crime against the Emperor.”

“The Emperor has declared all newly discovered Dwarven artifacts to be possessions of the Crown, which forbids their trade or sale. I’ll assume you were gifted that Dwemer shield and had no intention of trying to sell it. But you must set it aside before we talk trade.”
[/b][/center]

[u][b]East Empire Company[/b][/u]


You would think that East Empire Company(EEC)  members would expect you to hand in contraband on penalty of being reported to the guards, and I would agree with you. But the EEC members in the vanilla game (both Morrowind and Bloodmoon) who also offer bartering services, are not high ranking officials who would have the authority to collect contraband on behalf of the company. As such, service refusal is standard. Although a disposition drop will occur if you are in possession of raw glass or ebony and are not a member of either the EEC or the Legion.

[center]Player is EEC member:

[b]“You know I can't deal in raw glass, %PCRank. You'll have to hand that in to the Company.”[/b]

Player is in Legion:

[b]“I cannot deal in raw glass. You'll have to hand that in to the Company.”[/b]

Player is neither:

[b]“Why do you have raw glass in this bag!? This is the property of the Emperor. You should hand that in to a Company official if you don't want to face the penalty for smuggling.”[/b][/center]


[b][size=6][center][color=#ffe599]Extra Features[/color][/center][/size][/b]
[list]
[*]Many service NPCs will refuse to barter in corprus flesh and weepings, the exceptions being alchemists and apothecaries.
[/list][list]
[*]Publicans will also refuse to barter if you have vampire dust or human flesh.
[/list][list]
[*]Non-Temple NPCs in Vivec will not deal with you while you are carrying Inodril armor.
[/list]
[b][center]"Only the Temple can do dealings in sacred Indoril armor. %Name cannot risk her skin by trading with someone who carries it."[/center][/b][list]
[*]Added greetings to Temple members in Vivec city, commenting if you are wearing Indoril armor. These vary depending on your status but here is an example:
[/list]
[center][b]“I caution you, the Indoril armor you’re wearing is sacred to the Temple Ordinators. If they take umbrage, their justice will be swift and merciless.”[/b][/center]
[list]
[*]If you are arrested (pay gold or go to jail) you will now have contraband removed as well as stolen items. Thanks [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/38047?tab=user+files]abot[/url] for the script!
[/list][list]
[*]Service NPCs in the Legion will now alert the guards if you try to bring skooma or moonsugar to barter with them.
[/list][list]
[*]The Camonna Tong and the Thieves Guild as well as the two vanilla NPCs who sell Skooma and Moonsugar no longer refuse you trade for having those items.
[/list][list]
[*]As a non-East Empire Company member, handing in contraband voluntarily by walking up to an EEC official and selecting the topic “hand in contraband” will give you a very small cash reward (1 gold piece per contraband item). If you are a member of the East Empire Company or Legion and you hand in contraband, the reward will be significantly more, 5 gold pieces per item for Legionnaires and 10 gold per item for Company members.
[/list][list]
[*]The East Empire Company NPCs in Ebonheart were not technically part of the East Empire Company faction in the vanilla game, because that faction did not technically exist before the release of the Bloodmoon expansion, and they never bothered to fix it, so I have made it so these NPCs are now officially members and thus you can hand in your contraband to them if you wish. [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/36879320?tab=user+files]Half11[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/3241081?tab=user+files]Reizeron[/url] and I had fun figuring out what ranks they should be.
[/list][list]
[*]Fixed the bug mentioned [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:East_Empire_Company]here[/url] about the 0 alarm guards. This was done via a fire-once and then end startscript so it will work even if you are using mods that make changes to those NPCs.
[/list][list]
[*]Added some new dialogue for East Empire Company NPCs, introducing the “hand in contraband” topic and also referencing the Company’s Solstheim operations when the player is over level 5.
[*]Canctunian Ponius will no longer keep introducing himself after you've already met.
[/list]

[b][size=6][center][color=#ffe599]Text Changes
[/color][/center][/size][/b][list]
[*]Vanilla response to topic “East Empire Company”:
[/list]
[color=#ea9999]“The East Empire Company is a monopolistic merchantile enterprise charted by the Emperor and managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor. The Company has sole authority to trade in certain goods, like flin, raw ebony, raw glass, and Dwemer artifacts, and it also enjoys favorable tariffs and regulations for import and export of other common and exotic goods, like kwama eggs, marshmerrow pulp, saltrice, and Telvanni bug musk.“[/color]

This mod changes it to:

[color=#b6d7a8]“The East Empire Company is a monopolistic mercantile enterprise chartered by the Emperor and managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor. The Company has sole authority to trade in certain goods, raw ebony, raw glass, and Dwemer artifacts, and it also enjoys favorable tariffs and regulations for import of things like flin and export of other common and exotic goods, like kwama eggs, marshmerrow pulp, saltrice, and Telvanni bug musk.“[/color]

Not only does this fix two typos, it also specifies that flin is brought in from Cyrodiil and that it is not illegal for the player to trade in. I do not believe it was the developers' intent to make flin a restricted item and I am unaware of any other dialogue that might suggest it is. If anyone knows otherwise, please let me know.

[list]
[*]New variations of this line specifically for Legion and Imperial Cult members:
[/list]
[color=#b6d7a8]“The East Empire Company is the mercantile enterprise chartered by the Emperor and managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor himself. The Company has sole authority to trade in raw ebony, raw glass, and Dwarven artifacts. They have offices in Ebonheart and Fort Frostmoth.”[/color]

And for the East Empire Company:

[color=#b6d7a8]“We are the mercantile enterprise chartered by the Emperor and managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor himself. The Company has sole authority to trade in raw ebony, raw glass, and Dwarven artifacts. We have offices here and at Fort Frostmoth on Solstheim.”[/color] (Last sentence varies depending on NPC’s location)

[list]
[*]2x end sentences of vanilla journal entry IC13_rich (From Imperial Cult quest “Donation from Cunius Pelelius”):
[/list]
[color=#ea9999]“If I sell these pieces of raw ebony, I should be able to get 500 gold and more to deliver to Iulus Truptor for the Widows and Orphans Fund”[/color]

Changed to a more euphemistic tone with the goal to work with a broader range of role-playing styles:

[color=#b6d7a8]“If someone were to sell these pieces of raw ebony illegally, they might fetch 500 gold or more.”[/color]

name: FMI - Legion Dialogue
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Fixes several inconsistencies in dialogue spoken by members of the Imperial Legion.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link: 
[/b][/size][size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695 [/url]**[/b][/size]

This module of my ongoing "Inconsistencies" module of my ongoing "Finished Morrowind" project addresses the following inconsistencies in Imperial Legion dialogue:

[b][u][color=#ea9999]Issue 01[/color]
[/u][/b]
Imperial Guards and Legion members in Gnisis (including General Darius) talk about the Egg Mine being closed as though they are not the ones who are enforcing its closure, saying the same line as none-Legion NPCs in town: "It's up on the hill, on the east side of town. Careful in there, the kwama queen has been blighted. They're only letting miners in.” 

[b][u][color=#93c47d]Solution[/color]

[/u][/b]Members of the Legion will now tell you: “It's up on the hill, on the east side of town. Because the kwama queen has been blighted we are only granting access to miners at this time.”

If the player is in the Legion (and wearing the uniform as of 1.1) the line for Legion members and other NPCs will be: “It's up on the hill, on the east side of town. Careful in there, the kwama queen has been blighted.”

[b][u][color=#ea9999]Issue 02[/color]

[/u][/b]When doing the Imperial Legion quest that requires you to get the Gnisis Egg Mine key from the Legion guard (Vatollia Apo) outside it, he will hand over the key to you if you are in the Legion, saying:

"Since you're in the Legion, here's the key. Be careful."

The problem is he will say this even if you have been expelled from the Legion.

[b][u][color=#93c47d]Solution[/color]

[/u][/b]Now the key line (topic: eggmine) is filtered for PC Expelled !=1 which means you will have to re-join the Legion before Vatollia Apo will say that line.

[b][u][color=#ea9999]Issue 03[/color][/u][/b]

Legion NPCs still ask why you are out of uniform, why you are away from your post and generally address you as though you are a member of the Legion after you’ve been expelled.

[b][u][color=#93c47d]Solutions[/color]

[/u][/b]Greeting 1 line: "You're out of uniform. Talk to me when you're serious." now filtered for PC Expelled = 0

Hello lines: "At ease", "Your bidding Sir/Knight/Agent/Trooper?" and "This is truly an honor." now filtered for PC Expelled != 1

Hello line: "How dare you show your face." now filtered for PC Expelled = 1 (the vanilla filtering of ExpImperialLegion = -3 meant you could continue to hear the line "Why are you away from your post?" even after being expelled)

Added new response to topic "Imperial Legion" for if the player is expelled. Instead of: "For the glory of Tiber Septim, you and I should be honored to be in its service."
or giving you information on the Legion that you would probably already know if you had been a member, NPCs will simply respond with:
"For the glory of Tiber Septim, it is an honor to be in its service."
If you get expelled twice and are beyond the point of making amends, General Darius will say:
"For the glory of Tiber Septim, it is an honor to be in its service. Although clearly this is something that *you* do not understand." (Filtered for PC Expelled = 1 and ExpImperialLegion > 0)

[u][b][color=#ea9999]Issue 04[/color]

[/b][/u]The most common text greeting for Legion NPCs fails to acknowledge the player’s membership. The line remains: “I'm an officer of the Imperial Legion. Move along.” even if the player is also an officer of the Legion and even if you are the Knight of the Imperial Dragon.

[u][b][color=#93c47d]Solution[/color]

[/b][/u]Added a simple text greeting, addressing the player by their rank, this works for all ranks in the Legion until you are Knight of the Imperial Dragon, at which point Legion NPCs will greet you with "Hail to the Knight of the Imperial Dragon!"
These are also filtered to revert to vanilla should the player character be expelled.

[b][u][center]1.1 Update[/center][center]﻿[/center][/u][/b][color=#ea9999][b][u]Issue 05

[/u][/b][/color]Vatollia Apo gives you the key freely if you are in the Legion but if you talk to him about the egg mine again he says "I already gave you the key, now get lost before they see us talking." and you get a disposition drop even if you have already started the quest where Darius sends you to the mine. Dialogue from Lugrub gro-Ogdum updates to reflect your authority to be in the mine but Vatollia's does not.

[b][u][color=#93c47d]Solution[/color][/u][/b]

Now if you have started the quest IL_GnisisBlight, Vatollia will simply say "I already gave you the key." with no disposition drop.

name: FMI - Athyn and Shardie
author: PoodleSandwich
description: Makes Athyn Sarethi and Shardie's appearances more closely match what is inferred from the in-game book "The Hope of the Redoran".
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]** Please Note this mod is no longer updated on this page. For the most up-to-date version, follow this link: 
[/b][/size][size=4][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55695 [/url]**[/b][/size]

From "[url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Lore:The_Hope_of_the_Redoran]The Hope of the Redoran[/url]":

"Many, many years ago, a male child was born into House Redoran"

The boy was named Andas.

"His worst enemy was his cousin [b]Athyn[/b], who had borne much abuse at the hands of Andas."

"[b]Athyn [/b]had been sent to Rihad to complete his education"

"When [b]Athyn [/b]returned from [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Lore:Hammerfell]Hammerfell[/url], it was because of the death of his father, who had also been a councilor of the House. [b]Athyn [/b]was old enough to take his seat in the Council"

"[b]Athyn [/b]exercised his right to combat his cousin for the seat."

"[b]Athyn [/b]and his friends were discussing the duel morosely when one of his old teachers, a warrior called Shardie, came into the hall. "

[center]---------------------------------------------------[/center]

The book seems to infer that the Redguard named Shardie was an accomplished fighter and teacher before Athyn Sarethi was old enough to take his seat in the Council of House Redoran. 

I do not know exactly how old is old enough to take a seat in the Council, if anyone does please let me know, but it seems to me that Athyn was a relatively young man during the events of this book. 

As far as I know Redguards have pretty much IRL human life expectancy, whereas [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Interview_with_a_Dark_Elf]Dunmer live much longer[/url]﻿. 

In game, Shardie appears as a young woman and Athyn as a very old man, this seems highly unlikely to me so this mod changes their faces to better match the lore behind the characters, Athyn now appears younger and Shardie appears old.

Four out of the five times that male Redguards speak the word "Dunmer", Michael Mack pronounces it "Dumb-ner".

[i](Before you start quoting lore about historical rivalries between the two races; it happens on the high disposition greetings as well, and the only time he gets it right is on one of the lowest disposition greetings for when the player character is Dunmer.)
[/i]
So I took to Audacity to try and fix it. This was like trying to thread a needle with a sledge hammer.

I reached out to Mr. Mack to see if he would be interested in re-recording the lines. He didn't respond.

So finally I decided to go at it hammer and tongs with Adobe Audition and a demo version of Rx7 Advanced. This did the trick.

author: Maars
description: Adds new voiced lines recognizing your rank in Tamriel Rebuilt & Project Tamriel factions, including the new House Indoril faction from TR.
usage_notes:
Something I've always been interested in making ever since the Voice Generator came out, this mod adds voiced Hello lines (the ones NPCs that play when you get close to them) for the ranks of the unique joinable factions from PT and TR.

By unique I mean not simply localized equivalents of vanilla factions, like the province Mages and Fighters Guilds, as those are covered already by TD using the existing Mournhold lines.

If you use the main version of my [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59546]Vanilla Voices Unlocked[/url] mod the lines might not have enough priority to show up, so on its page I've added an alternate version that only includes the faction-related greetings, just like this mod.

These are the currently supported factions, with more to come as PTR adds new ones:
- [b]House Indoril[/b] (Dunmer M+F, Imperial M+F, as per existing House lines)
- [b]Ja-Natta Syndicate[/b] (Argonian F, Dunmer M+F, Orc M, these only play if the NPC is also part of the JNS)
- [b]Kingdoms of Anvil, Sutch, Kvatch[/b] (Imperial M+F)
- [b]Thieves Guild[/b] (Dunmer M+F, Imperial M+F)

[i]Small note[/i]: instead of the usual male dunmer AI voice you've gotten used to for dialogue mods (meant for easy cloning in longer lines), I've actually made my own from the Tribunal mp3s, which in my opinion makes the lines sound much closer to the vanilla voice. This should make the new lines weave more seamlessly with the existing ones.

Requirements:
- Tamriel Data [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59927]HD[/url]/[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44537]SD[/url] (technically doesn't need either PC or TR, but how would you join without them 😜)

Enjoy!

name: Great Service
author: Von Djangos
description: Enables voiced dialogue for shopkeepers that were shipped with the original game but never used.
usage_notes:
Enables over 100 lines of voiced dialogue for shopkeepers that were shipped with the original game but never used.

Although all races and genders recorded lines of dialogue for shopkeepers, for some reason Beth only ended up using the male lines for Dunmer, Altmer and Bretons in the original game.

This mod enables all other races, plus the female lines for Dunmer, Altmer and Bretons.

Beth buried the lines from the original three somewhat, so you wont hear them very often. I've surfaced mine higher in the list, so you're likely to hear them in the way you hear tavern owners or caravaneers say their lines.

Not all shopkeepers will use them, as there are many kinds of shopkeeper and some races don't have specific lines. For instance, Wood Elves recorded lines for being clothiers, and Khajit recorded lines for selling potions and books.

In short, it's abit of a grab bag - beth clearly didn't do a lengthy recording pass for some of the races - but you'll still hear quite alot of new voices by the original actors in the game now. Enjoy!
[b]
1.2 Update[/b]
I did a Todd and missed out on Imperial male and Argonian female voices when I did the original mod! This update adds them in.
I've also added in new ElevenAI voices for Nord women and Breton men for unrecorded classes like smiths, publicans, alchemists, etc
I'll add more of these in future updates.

name: Sheep-no-More
author: McChuggernaut
description: There are no sheep in Morrowind, so why should you be hearing them? This fixes that.
usage_notes:
Walking through the Ashlands near Ald Ruhn on a beautiful clear day, I was startled by a very loud and obvious sheep bleat that came out of nowhere. It broke my immersion pretty hard. There are no sheep in Morrowind, and I don't think anything else living in the region sounds like that. Besides, the audio file is a VERY obvious recording of a living sheep, not some distorted or human-made noise that might pass for a fantasy world sound. So, I took appropriate measures and replaced the culprit audio file with a re-named copy of another ambient creature sound from that region which was already in the game. I chose a somewhat quiet noise, since it will be occurring slightly more often in-game than it did before, and I didn't want it to be a loud, obvious sound that would be noticeably repetitive.

So yes, just replace the old sound file with the new one, and you get a sheep-free copy of Morrowind. Enjoy!

name: LDM - Balmora Rumour Fix
author: Lucevar
description: Adds an option to refuse Larrius Varro's Bloodbath quest, and edits the filtering on vanilla Balmora rumours so that they don't get overwritten by the Varro rumours. 16+ rumours now appear!
usage_notes:
[center][b]Balmora Rumour Fix + Varro quest refusal[/b]
by Lucevar[/center]

Did you know that Balmora actually has a LOT of responses for the latest rumours topic? Yeah, me neither. The only thing you ever hear about is Larrius Varro and his beef with the Camonna Tong. And since you can't avoid hearing about it, and you also can't turn the quest down, it will just sit in your journal forever if you don't want to do the quest (eg if you're roleplaying a pacifist or a Dunmer nationalist type character).

Well, not any more!

[b]Balmora Rumour Filters[/b]
Instead of the ~4 rumours you hear in vanilla, 16 general rumours are now available, plus lots of faction and NPC specific rumours (try talking to members of House Hlaalu, Heddvild, or Only-He-Stands-There, for example) that got drowned out by the Varro rumours. The Varro rumours will still appear, just MUCH less frequently. Some rumours will only appear once you've progressed past a certain point in the main quest. 

[b]Little Secret filters[/b]
There is an optional esp that changes the filtering on the 'little secret' dialogue of several NPCs who tell you Larrius Varro is looking for you, so that it will only appear if you have a reputation >= 6. Use INSTEAD OF the main esp. 

The NPCs are:
[list]
[*]Bacola Closcius
[*]Ranis Athrys
[*]Fascile Charascel
[*]Traven Marvos
[*]Benunius Agrudilius
[/list]
[b]Larrius Varro's Bloodbath - Quest Options[/b]
This mod also adds the option to turn down Varro's quest. He'll still tell you his little story, and you can still complete the quest by dealing with the bad people later - it just won't clutter up your journal. 

[b]Twin Lamps Legion Rumour[/b]
Finally, there was a rumour about the Twin Lamps assigned to members of the Imperial Legion in Balmora. By default, there aren't any members of the Legion in Balmora, so I assigned that rumour to Moonmoth Legion Fort instead. Requires a reasonably high rank in the Legion (Agent), and a disposition of 50, since the dialogue involves Legionaires admitting some sympathy towards an illegal organisation. 

Change log
===================================
Version 1.0
- Initial release.

name: LDM - Context Matters
author: Lucevar
description: Edits, re-filters, or adds on to vanilla dialogue to add more situational nuance - tavern owners will no longer talk about themselves in third person, Ashlanders will no longer curse vampires in the name of Almsivi, slave owners won't talk lovingly about abolitionists, and thieves will be less blase about incriminating themselves to strangers.
usage_notes:
[center][b][size=6]LDM - Context Matters

[/size][/b][/center][left]This mod is an attempt to fix one of the largest issues with Morrowind's dialogue: because the developers didn't have years to sit there and write dialogue to cover every possible scenario, there are places in the vanilla game where NPCs will talk about themselves in third person, casually incriminate themselves, swear by gods they don't believe in, or give replies completely unfitting for their status in life - uneducated paupers shouldn't give the same replies as savants!

Context Matters attempts to improve this situation by editing filters or adding new lines of dialogue more in keeping with the NPC's faith, class, race, faction, physical location, as well as quest completion status.

The mod is perfectly useable as is, but because of the scale of the game should be considered as-yet incomplete and very likely to be updated in the future as I find more jarring dialogue. As such, I will very happily take suggestions - contact me in the comments, in PM, or on Discord.

[u]NEW IN 1.4:[/u]
[size=3][b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48702]LDM - Ashlanders[/url]﻿[/b] now included: Yakum Hairshashishi will no longer flip between normal speech and broken ashlander speech. Ashlander scouts will no longer talk as though they're not Ashlanders themselves. Nibani Maesa will now react to you having Corprus. Zainab miners now have some unique greetings.

Several minor tweaks to little advice, Pelagiad greetings, Gnisis greetings, my trade. Filter fix for specific place in Ebonheart. Some new Ashlander-style responses to disease topics for wise women. Added no-lore filters to vampire topics.[/size]


[b][size=4][u]NEW IN 1.3:[/u][/size][/b]
Edited versions of[b] FMI - Ingredient Locations, FMI - Disease Descriptions,[/b] and[b] FMI - Misc [/b]dialogue consistency changes have been merged in (gameplay and creature tweaks ARE NOT included). Thank you, PoodleSandwich!
 
[b]Disease Descriptions[/b] - the most extensive changes in 1.3. On top of FMI's consistency changes, which removed references to creatures which don't carry disease in vanilla, I have added more personality to disease descriptions. There are four NPCs who talk about diseases in vanilla; two are professional healers, one is a well-traveled pilgrim, and one is a former Ashlander wise woman who now lives in Vos. Their new lines reflect their differing training, perspectives, and personalities.

[size=4][b][u]FEATURES INCLUDE:[/u][/b][/size]
[b]Abolitionists[/b] - Plantation owners now have disapproving responses when asked about abolitionists. Originally from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47499]LDM - Abolitionists[/url]﻿

[b]Ashlanders[/b] - Now no longer curse vampires in the name of Almsivi. Wise Women now have extra dialogue about vampires. Ashlander scouts will no longer talk as though they're not Ashlanders. 

[b]Balmora[/b] - Extra class and faction based responses to the 'Balmora', 'Bacola Closcius', and 'South Wall' topics. Better 'little advice' filtering. If you haven't started the main quest (eg if you're using an alternate start mod), asking about Caius Cosades at the South Wall will no longer trigger the main quest journal entries unless you have the Package for Caius in your inventory..

[b]Crassius Curio[/b] - [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47284]This mod[/url]﻿ is now included in Context Matters. Crassius Curio now has a variety of flirtatious voice lines if the player is naked. 

[b]Gnisis[/b] - Adds class/race/faction/quest responses to a number of topics, including greetings, 'Gnisis', 'Hetman Abelmawia', 'Widow Vabdas', 'Optio Bologra'.

[b]Ebonheart[/b] - Agning will no longer talk about himself in third person.

[b]Khuul[/b] - Location-based dialogue tweaks: NPCs in Thongar's Tradehouse will no longer respond as though they're standing on the docks instead.

[b]my trade[/b] - Odral Helvi will no longer tell you that he's a monk trained in Khajiiti martial arts, because that makes no sense. He now informs you that he oversees House Hlaalu's affairs in Caldera instead.

[b]Seyda Neen[/b] - Eldafire will now be less ungrateful if you clear out Addamasartus. Asking Elone the Scout about Balmora will no longer trigger a main-quest journal update if you haven't already started the main quest (eg if you're using an alternate start mod). Some little advice responses which previously were filtered to occur in Seyda Neen but were never seen because no NPCs of the appropriate class exist there will now trigger elsewhere as well.

[b]Telvanni[/b] - Adds extra variety to vampire greetings.

[b]Thieves[/b] - Refilters the little advice topic for thieves, so that they save their most incriminating advice for fellow members of the Thieves Guild. Dialogue in Balmora which previously directed the player to seek out the Thieves Guild regardless of identity will now only be given to players with a bounty.

[b]Vampires[/b] - Context Matters includes [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47556]LDM - Vampire Talk[/url]﻿, adding more variety to vampire greetings for Telvanni, Ashlanders, necromancers, and some individual NPCs, and other vampirism related topics are expanded on or tweaked as well.

name: Honorable Dagoth - Courtesy of the First Blow
author: Sweezly
description: Dagoth Ur will keep his fucking word.
usage_notes:
Through several dialogue lines, Dagoth Ur offers to let you deliver the first hit on him before your fight, only to turn immediately hostile and chuck a fireball at you. This could be interpreted as him playing dirty, and that he's actually just a bastard who will use whatever means to grasp at victory, sure... In that case, why let you hit him at all then? He's not immediately hostile after all, and it's not like he isn't a God (how can you kill a God?).

I think more than anything that this was just an oversight on Bethesda's part, a leftover script from the cut behavior of other ash vampires where they'd only turn hostile after you engaged in dialogue with them.

The mod removes the 'setfight 100' script that activates during his dialogue, meaning the man is now [s]completely docile[/s] entirely [i]honorable. [/i]Relatively simple mod, perhaps too much so, but I haven't seen anyone care enough to address it, so there.

[u][size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size][/u]
Should be compatible with anything that doesn't edit Dagoth Ur's 'final questions' dialogue topic, and I doubt any mods do.
