description: Curated compilation of 600+ unique, vanilla-friendly designs for unique vanilla objects
usage_notes:
[center][u][b][size=5]Unique Uniques[/size][/b][/u]
[size=4]By: Anumaril21[/size][/center]

﻿


[u]Contents:[/u]

I. Requirements
II. Description
III. Compatibility
IV. Installation and Removal
V. Permissions
VI. Credits

[u]I. Requirements:[/u]

- Morrowind
- Tribunal
- Bloodmoon

[u]II. Description:[/u]

Over the years, many community members have attempted to partially address the lack of unique appearances for unique armor, weapons, creatures, and miscellaneous items within Morrowind. These efforts were never completed and could be difficult to track down between minor mod pages and lost MMH content; not to mention many were high-fidelity, and weren't a good fit for vanilla purists like myself. I've taken the effort to track down, curate, and edit what designs I could find to blend them as seamlessly as I could with the vanilla game; avoiding simple reskins to the best of my ability in favor of designs that add unique geometry or other interesting aspects like animations. What items were missing, or had clashing/dated designs, myself and others in the community went ahead and created new looks for. Additionally, some vanilla items that shared models with unrelated items were given their own appearance. Where possible, assets were recreated using MOP/Clothing Ground Mesh Fix models as a base, while Creature VFX Restoration fixes were forwarded. 

What's Included: Unique designs for 600+ unique and some named/near-unique armor, weapons, books, lights, potions, ingredients, clutter, and creatures that had generic appearances. Female models are provided for all added cuirasses. A complete list of these with credits is available in the docs section and in the download.

There is also an option for 'More Unique Uniques', these are unique items in Morrowind that had their own models, but have been improved upon in minor ways through animations, particle effects, glowmaps, or edited geometry. These include:

[list]
[*]Auriel's Shield[/*]
[*]Chrysamere[/*]
[*]Daedric Crescent[/*]
[*]Ebony Mail[/*]
[*]Eltonbrand[/*]
[*]Fang of Haynekhtnamet[/*]
[*]Goldbrand[/*]
[*]Iceblade of the Monarch[/*]
[*]Keening[/*]

[*]Scourge[/*]
[*]Spear of Bitter Mercy[/*]
[*]Spell Breaker[/*]
[*]Staff of Hasedoki[/*]
[*]Staff of Magnus[/*]
[*]Sunder[/*]
[*]Umbra[/*]
[/list][u]III. Compatibility:[/u]

This mod largely changes models and icons for various vanilla objects, with some placement editing where necessary, and should be compatible with most other mods that don't edit the same elements or make drastic changes to the locations they're placed in. Mods changing item stats should be compatible, with any issues that arise being fixable with a multipatch/merged objects. 'More Unique Uniques' simply replaces the models for most vanilla artifacts, save the Ebony Mail, which is edited to include a female model, if that isn't of interest to you, the .esp can be disabled. Just make sure these .esp load after other mods which may alter any of these items, and it's placed lower in your mod organizer than mods that touch them like MOP or Patch for Purists.

Built-In Compatibility:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46599]Graphic Herbalism[/url]


[u]IV. Installation and Removal:[/u]

To install, make sure you first have the dependencies listed, then use the mod manager of your choice.

To remove, simply delete the associated files through said mod manager.

[u]V. Permissions[/u]

This mod is intended to be both a somewhat definitive uniques mod as well as a community resource, as it wouldn't exist without the community. If you're interested in contributing new items, improvements, sheathes, or optimizations feel free to DM me or find me on Discord. Included in the download and docs section is a complete item-by-item credits list. You are free to use and adapt any assets contained here so long as the relevant creators are credited. I've worked on this between projects for years now, so I would appreciate if my work wasn't reuploaded into another compilation, but rather others work with me on this one. You're on your honor.

-Part 2 of 3 of my rebalance series-

This mod is intended to rebalance the Bloodmoon expansion in a variety of ways, most importantly by editing the stats of creatures and npcs.
This mod rebalances Bloodmoon as if it shipped with Morrowind.

[Intro]
Tribunal and Bloodmoon were released as expansions to the base game, and were intended for players who had already fully cleared previous quests. All of the enemies and non-hostile NPCs are much higher level because of that. While a powerful vanilla NPC might be level 30, a powerful Bloodmoon NPC could be level 70. Ash Vampires and 'legendarily powerful' creatures/NPCs in the base game are somehow weaker than most expansion NPCs.

Parts 1 and 3 of the rebalance series (in progress) tackle Tribunal, and finally making the 6th House / Dagoth Ur terrifying entities that even the most powerful Bloodmoon Skaal couldn't defeat easily.

The general theory for these Bloodmoon changes are as follows:

-Wolves and bears should be 'tough creatures like kagouti' not 'berserk killing machines'
-Werewolves are HP sponges (they shouldn't be)
-The end dungeon for BM is not fun
-Rieklings should be weaker than most standard humans. Low level characters should have no problems killing a riekling or two.
-Riekling weapons/armor should be low quality, not expensive and amazing
-Non riekling item stats/placement is untouched
-The bell curve for Bloodmoon NPCs peaks at around 25. It is a harsh landscape and weak people would not survive.
-Level 40 is the 'high limit' for standard humanoid races.
-Level 50 is the limit for npcs with extreme magical powers or special circumstances (Hunt NPCs, Witches)

This Bloodmoon Rebalance will put the Bloodmoon Main Quest about on par with Tribunal's. The landscape will be much less challenging than it was before. The creatures and NPCs now fit roughly in the vanilla Morrowind progression. You could visit at level 1 and complete the Bloodmoon main quest at level 30 if you're well equipped.

[Changes]
I have separated my changes into a few categories to provide a modular approach. These changes are also packaged into one esp if you'd like all of my changes.

Bloodmoon Creature rebalance.esp
Bears, wolves, and horkers are now much weaker
riekling lance / sword / are now worthless and also bad
all rieklings / bristlebacks are much weaker
spriggans are slightly weaker and don't have grand souls anymore
Grahl are slightly weaker
The Swimmer / The Good Beast have lowered HP slightly but that doesn't affect much

Bloodmoon Undead Rebalance.esp
bonewolves and draugr are now weaker and have weaker souls
draugr are now undead (before they were creatures)
draugr lord aesliip HP and level lowered
skeletons slightly reduced HP

Bloodmoon Boss Rebalance.esp
Edits "boss" creatures / NPCs that may affect the endgame balance
Udyrfrikke / lightkeeper grahl / karstaag are slightly weaker (reduced HP, they still do some crazy damage)
falx carius and tharsten heart-fang maze forms now lower leveled slightly (20% less health)

Bloodmoon Werewolf Rebalance

Maze werewolves now have 200 health instead of 700 because I hate the maze with a burning passion. There are 31 of them in the final dungeon. No one has time for that.

name: MDMD - More Deadly Morrowind Denizens
author: autumn
description: 230+ NPCs are given unique spells, enchantments, and items, to make Morrowind deadlier AND more varied. Faction bosses, Artifact owners, and Daedric cultists have been given customized, flavorful make-overs to become more difficult AND more memorable. Players are encouraged to carry resists, dispels, restores, and prepare ahead for big fights.
usage_notes:
[]--------------------------------------------------[]
||More Deadly Morrowind Denizens||
[]--------------------------------------------------[]

MDMD is a balance mod inspired by mortimermcmire's Sixth House/Tribunal/Bloodmoon rebalance series and the Morrowind Anti-Cheese mod. This began as an attempt to make the Vvardenfell boss characters feel like actual bossfights, and has ballooned into a full rebalance, making enemies who were meant to be powerful as dangerous and unique as they should be.

When Bethesda made Morrowind, they clearly thought level 20 was as high as a player character would ever get. The most powerful enemies in Vvardenfell tend to clock in around level 20 themselves, despite high-level player characters tending to land around level 30 or above. They realized this was wrong, and overcompensated in Tribunal and Bloodmoon. mortimermcmire fixed that, but this is intended to fix the original mistake with Morrowind.

This mod affects certain faction quest targets, Daedric shrine cultists, non-6th House Dunmer Strongholds, Artifact owners, and faction bosses. Only character stats/items/spell-lists have been changed, not location.

230+ NPCs are modified. 140+ NPC-only spells are added to increase spellcaster variety. 85 uniquely-enchanted items spice up your opponents' options.

Enemies are not just increased in level--they are given unique spell-lists and enchantments based on who they are, where they are, and who they work for. They are given tricks that belong to them alone, making each fight a more unique, memorable encounter.

Daedra Shrines and Dunmer Strongholds are now level ~20 challenges. Cultists of different lords use different strategies. Worshipers of Malacath will hit you with curses; Mehrunes Dagon's boys will overload you with destructive force; Molag Bal's cultists will Paralyze you and torment you with slow-acting torture; Sheogorath's own will come at you with unpredictable tricks. The Redoran of Marandus have enchantments granting them the protection of their ancestors. The bandits of Andasreth make use of a wild collection of scrolls, enchanted items, and other desperate tricks! etc.,

Your Great House Rivals in Bal Isra, Rethan Manor, and Tel Uvirith have gone from being push-overs to full-fledged bossfights with their own unique fighting styles, and access to their factions' exclusive rewards! The Redoran rival is no longer unarmed, but fully geared, and protected by his ancestors with each blow he strikes. The Hlaalu rival has sneaky tricks to disable you and leave you helpless. Tremble in fear at the Telvanni rival's unparalleled rainbow magic and mastery of Dwemer animunculi!

Artifact owners are turned into level 30 bosses, each with new, unique tricks. Sorkvild the Raven, a necromancer, now WEARS the Masque of Clavicus Vile, and summons an army of undead while blasting you with the cold of the grave. Dreveni Hlaren, owner of the Staff of Magnus, now summons a full suit of Bound Armor and will turn your Drain Health tricks back on YOU! etc.,

Faction final bosses are now level 40, and menace with new tricks of their own. Archmagister Gothren can summon even more Dremora, and his offensive magic will teach you why he's on top. Sjoring Hard-Heart now wears some of the best armor around, and his unique hammer powers him up while tearing you down. etc.,

Vampire Ancients are now level 50, and present challenges even to a powerful Nerevarine. Quake in terror at the unrivaled power of Aundae's magic. Run like prey while Berne strikes at you from the shadows with impunity. Die horribly while Quarra butchers you alive with her new axe.

Player characters will now have a reason to prepare for dangerous fights. Stock up on Resist Element, Resist/Cure Paralysis, Restore Attribute, and Dispel options. Enemies will use effects against you they rarely did before. Be prepared to be Blinded, struck with long-lasting poisons, and--yes--to have 1pt Levitation cast on you, forcing you to float around helplessly. They can do that now. They will do that now.

I've spent ~15 hours testing the balance of this mod, but Morrowind is, in fact, a very difficult game to balance. Clever players might still roll over the challenges here. More natural players might find this all very difficult. I am open to feedback about things that need improvement.

[]----------------[]
||Modularity||
[]----------------[]

If this is too much for you, use MDMD - Bosses, which only affects the bosses of faction questlines and Artifact owners. It reduces it down to 36 characters only.

If this isn't enough for you, MDMD - Creatures, modifies the spell-lists of many monsters. The curses the Undead cast on you are now more dangerous and consistent. The lowly Bonewalker damages your Luck; the Greater Bonewalker does much more reasonable, reduced Strength damage than before; the Bonelord damages your Speed and Agility! The Hunger had a Paralyze it never used--now all its Distintergrate and Paralyze spells are wrapped up into one deadly spell-package! The non-summoned Dremora will now summon help of their own; lesser Dremora calling on Clannfear, Dremora Lords calling in their own Dremora lackey!


[]----------------------------[]
||Compatibility & Etc||
[]----------------------------[]

This mod has been cleaned with EnchantedEditor.


This mod will conflict with any mod that modifies the altered characters' spell-lists, inventories, or stats. Whichever mod is loaded last will override the changes of the other. I'm willing to mess around to make compatibility patches if anyone has any requests. A full list of every single NPC and how they are changed is included so you can set up your load-order or set your compatabilities as needed. If you make compatability mods between this and other mods that's great too go ahead do my work for me thank you kindly.

This mod is fully compatible with mortimermcmire's rebalance series, it does not touch anything it touches. I strongly recommend them.

This mod changes many characters Morrowind Anti-Cheese changes, but does not do a lot of what it otherwise does. Load MDMD after Anti-Cheese, so MDMD overrides characters with the new spell-lists and enchanted items. In many cases, I've made artifact holders stronger than Anti-Cheese, if only by giving them more useful spell-lists. Anti-Cheese still fixes a ton of poor enchantment designs, spell-effects, exploits, etc, and is very much worth using.

This mod does not alter Umbra. Use MelchiorDarhk's fantastic Umbra mod for that.

name: Tamriel ReBalanced - Deadlier Denizens
author: KiraMW
description: Makes hostile Tamriel Rebuilt NPCs fight like they should, with specialized caster archetypes, custom spells, summons, stronger stats, and competent builds.
usage_notes:
[heading][center]TAMRIEL REBALANCED[/center]
[/heading]
[b]Tamriel ReBalanced is a dynamic NPC rebalance for Tamriel Rebuilt's hostile humanoids.[/b]

Using OpenMW Lua, the mod evaluates each NPC's existing [b]level and class[/b] and applies an appropriate package. Spellcasters gain specialized spell sets, defenses and abilities; martial characters receive improved attributes, skills and durability; hybrid classes are strengthened in both areas.

The strength of those changes is based on the NPC's existing TR level. A level 5 bandit receives a modest package intended for early characters. A level 20 warrior is built as an experienced combatant. A level 30 rogue mage can possess powerful magic and defenses appropriate to a rare late-game enemy.

Tamriel ReBalanced keeps TR's existing levels and encounters intact, but ensures hostile NPCs have competent builds that match their level and class. Encounter placement and NPC levels remain where TR put them.

This does [b]not[/b] make NPCs scale to the player's level, and it is not intended as a hardcore difficulty or challenge mod. The goal is simply to make hostile NPCs feel believable and competent, rather than the pushovers they can often be in vanilla TR.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662117-115946061.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]WHAT CHANGES?[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Spellcasters[/b] receive class-appropriate specializations with deliberately constructed spell sets, defenses and abilities.[/*]
[*][b]Martial characters[/b] receive level-appropriate improvements to their attributes, weapon skills, defensive skills and durability.[/*]
[*][b]Hybrid characters[/b] receive both martial and magical improvements appropriate to their class.[/*]
[/list]Dedicated spellcasters are an extensive part of the overhaul. They currently draw from [b]15 different specializations[/b], each built across six level bands for a total of [b]90 specialization and level combinations[/b].

A given Sorcerer, Mage, Warlock, Necromancer or Witch can therefore fight very differently from another member of the same class.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662142-787812940.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]MORE THAN BIGGER NUMBERS[/heading]
Tamriel ReBalanced is deliberately [b]not[/b] a blanket stat multiplier or health-bloat mod.

Health is increased where needed, but survivability is only one part of the rebalance. Weapon skills, defensive skills, attributes, spell selection, regeneration, summons, resistances and other abilities are adjusted according to what that character is supposed to be.
A high-level mage should not simply take longer to kill. They should be a [b]better mage[/b].

Caster archetypes are built as [b]coherent specializations[/b], each with its own offensive tools, defenses, summons or utility. Stronger versions are designed for higher-level NPCs.

Some examples include:
[list]
[*][b]Stormblood:[/b] Shock magic, atronachs and magical defenses.[/*]
[*][b]Daedric Vessel:[/b] Sacrifices its own health to summon increasingly dangerous Daedra.[/*]
[*][b]Antimage:[/b] Silence, Magicka damage and defenses against enemy spellcasters.[/*]
[*][b]Gravecaller:[/b] Overwhelms enemies with increasingly powerful groups of undead.[/*]
[*][b]Spellwright:[/b] Specializes in destroying weapons and armor.[/*]
[*][b]Abyssal Leech:[/b] Drains Health, Magicka, Fatigue and attributes from its enemies.[/*]
[/list]This means even enemies sharing the same base class can present substantially different problems in combat.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662157-1343864506.png[/img]
[line]
[heading]BUILT FROM TAMRIEL REBUILT[/heading]
Development began by examining Tamriel Rebuilt's actual NPC records. TR's hostile population was analyzed by [b]level, class, aggression, attributes, skills and combat role[/b]. Classes were separated into martial, caster and hybrid groups, and the resulting packages were built around the patterns already present in TR. This approach also closely follows Project Tamriel's own encounter-design guidance.

The guiding question was simple:

[b]If Tamriel Rebuilt says this character is level 20, what should a competent level 20 version of this character's class actually be capable of?[/b]
[line]
[heading][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60060/60060-1788662497-412922151.png[/img]
WHAT SHOULD I EXPECT?[/heading]
Early Tamriel Rebuilt remains approachable. Low-level enemies are more capable, but still appropriate for developing characters.

The difference becomes increasingly noticeable as enemy level rises. Mid-level combatants demand more respect, while TR's rare high-level enemies can finally become the serious threats their placement and level imply.

That also makes the world make more sense. When a village is worried about a dangerous necromancer occupying a nearby ruin, the answer is no longer necessarily, [i]"Why doesn't one of the guards just kill him?"[/i]

Sometimes that necromancer really is someone the guards would rather not fight.
[line]
[heading]SCOPE[/heading]
Tamriel ReBalanced dynamically modifies qualifying Tamriel Rebuilt humanoid combatants through OpenMW Lua. It does not change TR's quests, dialogue, locations or encounter placement, and makes no substantial changes to NPC inventories.

Enemies do not scale with the player.

NPCs above the mod's current level-30 rebalance range are left untouched.

Requires OpenMW.

name: Morrowind Quests Redux
author: Kildozery
description: A lightweight and vanilla-friendly revisit of Morrowind's questlines. This series aims to make them a more rewarding and enjoyable experience to play, whilst holding true to vanilla's vision.
usage_notes:
[size=3]Morrowind Quests Redux provides a refreshed and improved Vanilla+ questing experience, and does so whilst not getting carried away with any major changes to the original vision.

During my time exploring Vvardenfell I noticed that many quests don't reward the player at all for completing them. Some quests and/or factions also often lack reputation gains. And finally, some factions also reward the player almost exclusively in gold, which can quickly get repetitive. [/size]

[b][color=#6aa84f][size=5][center]Redux aims to fix this![/center][/size][/color][/b]

[b][color=#6aa84f][size=4]A note on balance:[/size][/color][/b]

[color=#b6d7a8][size=3]I've designed the balance of Redux with a few things in mind. Firstly I'm assuming that like me, players will be roleplaying a specific play style/archetype for each of their characters. If you do "it all" on a single character you'll likely be quite inundated with [b]lots[/b] of shiny loot (is this really any different from vanilla's end game anyway?). Secondly, I also balance around the difficulty/balance mods I recommend further down this page, so [i]some[/i] rewards are proportional to the difficulty increase from other mods like MDMD. The vast majority of added rewards however [b]are[/b] balanced in line with vanilla's precedent.

MQR is designed to compliment vanilla’s vision, not replace it. As such players should find everything more or less “feels” just like vanilla, just with subtle improvements. 

The vast majority of changes affect existing quests which previously awarded nothing to the player. And care has been taken to ensure new rewards are balanced, proportional, and don’t feel too “moddy”. Rewards also correlate to the factions favoured attributes and skills, to ensure they feel appropriate. [/size][/color]

name: The Missing Class - Mananaut
author: TwilotSpankle
description: There's a missing class in the class triangle, time to fill it!
usage_notes:
Every single vanilla class can be placed in a class triangle. Thief-oritented clases on one end, warrior on the 2nd, mages on the 3rd. 5 classes are perfectly situated in one of these 3 orientations, another 3 are perfect balances of 2, and then the bard is a perfect hybrid of all 3. These are entirely based on the skillset. EXAMPLES. The rogue has an equal number of thief and warrior skills, 5 warrior 5 thief, meaning it's a perfect balance of the two. Assassin's have 6 thief, 3 warrior, and 1 magic skill/s, meaning it's a thief-aligned class with a slight lean towards warrior, and a tad of magic. 

These classes have been mapped out on a class triangle before, I'm not the first to do so, but as far as I'm aware I'm the 1st to make an attempt to FILL IN this missing class that is magic oriented, with a slight lean towards warrior. Below is a list of every class, it's skillset make-up, and where the missing class fits in.

[spoiler]THIEF CLASSES
9 stealth, 1 combat, 0 magic: thief
6 stealth, 3 combat, 1 magic: assassin
6 stealth, 2 combat, 2 magic: acrobat
6 stealth, 1 combat, 3 magic: agent
5 stealth, 3 combat, 2 magic: monk
5 stealth, 2 combat, 3 magic: pilgrim

WARRIOR CLASSES
9 combat, 0 magic, 1 stealth: warrior
6 combat, 2 magic, 2 stealth: knight
6 combat, 1 magic, 3 stealth: barbarian
5 combat, 2 magic, 3 stealth: archer
5 combat, 3 magic, 2 stealth: crusader
4 combat, 3 magic, 3 stealth: scout

MAGE CLASSES
9 magic, 0 combat, 1 stealth: mage
6 magic, 3 combat, 1 stealth: battlemage
6 magic, 1 combat, 3 stealth: healer
6 magic, 2 combat, 2 stealth: sorcerer
5 magic, 2 combat, 3 stealth: witchhunter
[b]new class: either: 5 magic, 4 stealth, 1 combat
OR
4 magic, 3 stealth, 3 combat[/b]

PERFECT HYBRID CLASSES
3 combat, 3 magic, 3 stealth: bard
5 magic, 5 stealth, 0 combat: nightblade
5 combat, 5 stealth, 0 magic: rogue
5 magic, 5 combat, 0 stealth: spellsword[/spoiler]

Below is my reasoning behind every skill I've picked

[spoiler]Spear - Not a single damn class has a spear as a major skill. Once again spear lovers get the short end of the stick. I've made it a major skill
Medium and Light Armor - Douglass Goodall himself has made a mod, [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52896?tab=files&file_id=1000063775]The Mananaut's Message[/url][/b], which allows you to obtain "Royal Mananaut armor", which is light armor...HOWEVER, tamriel_data has a mananaut helmet which is medium armor and assumably future pieces will also be medium. So I chose both
Armorer - I needed more warrior-oriented skills, and I didnt want to overfill this class with a dozen offensive skills, and block doesnt make sense, so I chose armorer. Gotta repair your armor somehow on the moon...
Acrobatics - It's the moon. JUMPY JUMPY!!!!
Speechcraft - Mananaut's are a HELLA unique people to hang out with, when you talk with them you will always have your full attention on their words
All other magic skills - Because magic-oriented class of course[/spoiler]

[b][size=4]RECCOMENDED MODS

[/size][/b][size=3][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53710]ARCE All Races and Classes Enabled[/url] - More classes to play from vanilla and tamriel data! And all the cool new TD races of course. Naga Mananaut anyone?
[/size] 
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/47115]Sensible Races and BIrthsigns[/url] - I can't play without this mod. Makes slight tweaks to some races that just make sense (Argonians will no longer drown) and birthsigns, cause lets face it some birthsigns are just USELESS

[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59240]Prison Transfer Alternate Start[/url] - Now you start your character creation IN the imperial city prisons

name: Fairer Weapon and Magic Experience Gains for Sane People
author: MaxYari
description: Fairifies experience gains without overhauling them. Casting magica-expensive spells or using slow weapons brings more XP, failing a cast or missing a swing still grants a little as you learn from your mistakes. Using conjured gear grants a bit of conjuration XP.
usage_notes:
[size=6][b]✦ Fairer Magic and Weapon Experience Gains for Sane People[/b][/size]

A friendly adjustment of the way Magic and Weapon experience gains work. Doesnt aim to be an overhaul, but rather to simply illiminate some points of contention and unfairness, as well as reduce the dark-side pull of a common ways of exploiting the morrowind xp system for "effecient" skill leveling (quick attack spam, cheap "practice" spells). At the same time it's not an anti-cheese mod, previously "efficient" tactics are either slightly less efficient or as eficcient as before, BUT this mod makes normal skill use in combat more appealing and effective as a means of natural experience gain. The changes are quite succinct and are listed below:

[list]
[*][b]Magic XP scales with spell cost.[/b] Casting a spell that costs 15 or less magica grants 1x XP, while a spell costing 75 or more magica grants 5x XP.[/*]
[*][b]Slow weapons grant more XP per hit, fast ones less.[/b] A dagger hit teaches about 0.6x, a long sword 1.15x, a two-handed axe 1.3x, a bow 1.9x. The exact multiplier depends on a true weapon speed, which is different from the speed displayed in the game since different weapons have different actual speed at 1.0 speed value due to differences in their animation durations.[/*]
[*][b]Miscasts and misses still bring a little XP[/b] You do learn from your failures! Only 1/3 of xp that you would've gotten otherwise and, additionally this exp can not actually level up the skill, you still need to succeed atleast once to get over the level up threshold.[/*]
[*][b]Conjuration XP from bound gear and Alteration XP from shields[/b], being hit while under an Alteration shield or actively using a Conjured equipment - grants extra XP of the appropriate magic school.[/*]
[/list]
Adjustible in setting: Options -> Scripts -> Fairer Magic and Weapon XP.

[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img width=217]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/morrowind_kofi_banner_left_half_bright124.gif[/img][img width=618]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_right.png[/img][/url]
[url=https://ko-fi.com/maxyari][img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/main/imgs/nexus/banner_glow.png[/img][/url]

[size=5][b]✦ How to install[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Requires OpenMW 0.51 or newer.[/b][/*]
[*]Install and enable [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60256]Max Yari's Script Services (MSS)[/url], it's a required dependency.[/*]
[*]Install this mod [b]with a mod organiser[/b]: download the archive (or this repository as an archive) and drag and drop it into your mod organiser of choice (e.g [url=https://github.com/ModOrganizer2/modorganizer/releases]Mod Organizer 2[/url] on Windows or [url=https://github.com/grazelandsnomad/nerevarine_organizer/releases/tag/v0.70]Nerevarine Organizer[/url] on Linux). [b]Or[/b] [url=https://modding-openmw.com/tips/installing-mods/]read this tutorial[/url] on how to install mods using the launcher or completely manually (it's also very easy).[/*]
[*]Enable [font=Courier New]FairerMagicAndWeaponXP.omwscripts[/font] in the "Content Files" tab of the OpenMW launcher, after [font=Courier New]MaxYariScriptServices.omwscripts[/font].[/*]
[/list]
Safe to add to or remove from a game in progress.

[size=5][b]✦ Mod compatibility[/b][/size]

Don't combine it with other mods that scale magic or weapon experience (MBSP, Skill Uses Scaled, NCGDMW's magicka-based progression) - both would scale the same experience. Skill uncappers and level-up overhauls are fine.

Modders: how it works, and its interface, is in the [url=https://github.com/MaxYari/FairerWeaponAndMagicExpGainsOpenMW/blob/main/Sources/DEVELOPMENT.md]technical notes[/url].

[size=5][b]✦ AI disclaimer[/b][/size]

This mod is 95% AI slop, this kind of minor rebalance sounded like a great idea to me, especially in a context of my current playthough and I was not satisfied with the existing solutions (they are either too overloaded or just dont do what this mod does). I also had a paid slopmachine subscription at the time, so slopping this out was fairly straightforward. I am still using this in my playthrough and am quite satisfied with how sublte yet fair the changes are, so I think the mod deserved a right to not just be considered a mere slop. Cheers!

name: State-Based HP - Lua
author: degede
description: A conversion of "Talrivian's State-Based HP" to OpenMW Lua.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
original Morrowind script mod can be found [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/52183]here[/url]
[i]"Dynamically calculates your maximum Health based on your current Endurance, Strength, and level, removing the need to prioritize stat gains to maximize Health. The mod applies the vanilla Health formula, but uses current player stats."[/i]

'Talrivian's State-Based HP' had a couple subtle bugs and, being a standard script, provided no configurable options or feedback to help narrow down potential problems. I've re-implementation it in Lua for OpenMW.

Just like the original, this script updates the character's max health any time their strength, endurance, or level changes - using the formula:
( ( Strength + Endurance) / 2 ) + ( ( Endurance / 10 ) * ( Level - 1 ) )

This is essentially identical to the game's original health formula. (with only a minor difference arising from it being applied dynamically if you really want to dig into it)

Issues in the original script:
[list]
[*]How it handled fortify health effects was not correct.[/*]
[*]Health was not recalculated on level up if strength and endurance had not changed.[/*]
[*]Under some rare circumstances, the script would produce a health value that was noticeably lower than it should be (around 15% in a situation I was able to consistently reproduce). I didn't narrow down exactly what was going wrong, but the original script was heavily redundant and kind of messy. This no longer seems to be an issue with this new implementation.[/*]
[/list]What I changed from the original:
[list]
[*]Max health was immediately modified when fortifying or damaging endurance or strength. This is not desirable if you want as-vanilla-as-possible behavior, but some players may have liked that from the original. Strength now uses base value only. Endurance will always consider fortify effects from abilities like The Lady sign (this matches vanilla behavior), but whether or not it considers other fortify and damage effects is now an option.[/*]
[/list]
A simple script menu page is also included:
[list]
[*]toggle the script itself[/*]
[*]toggle if max health should be effected by all fortify/damage endurance effects[/*]
[*]toggle debug output[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[size=3][color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW[/color][/size]



[color=#D4D4D8]Thanks to Talrivian for the original mod and mikeprichard[/color] for uploading it to nexusmods.

name: State-Based Magicka Regen (SBMR) (OpenMW)
author: mym
description: SBMR dynamically makes all actors (player, creatures, NPCs) slowly regenerate their magicka based on their state: Willpower, intelligence, magicka, fatigue, encumbrance, movement, and specific magic effects.
usage_notes:
[size=5]State-Based Magicka Regen[/size]

[b]OpenMW 0.49 or above is required![/b]

[size=4]Features[/size]

[list]
[*]Magicka regeneration for the player, creatures, and NPCs[/*]
[*]Highly customizable regen rate based on each actor's state: Willpower, intelligence, magicka, fatigue, encumbrance, movement, sleeping, and specific magic effects[/*]
[*]Customizable regen rate with the Stunted Magicka effect (e.g. The Atronach birthsign) (0% regen by default)[/*]
[*]Customizable regen rate for actors regenerating their magicka (constant effect, potions...) (100% by default)[/*]
[*]Distinct regen rates for the player and other actors[/*]
[*]Supports regen during time passed while resting, waiting, traveling, training... for all actors, based on a customizable timescale setting[/*]
[*]Overrides vanilla regen after sleeping, traveling or a jail sentence, keeping what Restore Magicka effects gave[/*]
[*]Supports regen for inactive actors becoming active again after some time[/*]
[*]Shows player's current regen and factor values in the settings[/*]
[*]Shows current regen value in the player stats window's magicka tooltip when the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57727]Stats Window Extender[/url] mod is installed[/*]
[*]Minimal impact on FPS and game save size (scripts only attached to actors who are active and lack magicka, checks done once per second)[/*]
[/list][size=4]What It Does[/size]

SBMR dynamically makes all actors (player, creatures, NPCs) slowly regenerate their magicka based on their state: Willpower, intelligence, magicka, fatigue, encumbrance, movement, sleeping, and specific magic effects.

Default regen settings:

[list]
[*]Make actors regen 2.5 times faster than the player, because they rarely use restore magicka potions[/*]
[*]Make the long periods of time spent (resting, traveling...) use a timescale of 30[/*]
[*]Set a regen based on willpower (20% for the player, 50% for other actors), altered by:

[list]
[*]Intelligence (50% to 150%)[/*]
[*]Fatigue (50% to 100%)[/*]
[*]Encumbrance (50% to 100%)[/*]
[*]Movement (walk at 75%, run at 50%)[/*]
[*]Sleeping (200%)[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*]Prevents regen for actors with the Stunted Magicka[/*]
[/list]When selecting Magicka as the regen main stat, the used value excludes magicka fortifications.

[size=4]Configuration[/size]

Settings allow you to select a base stat that will be used to compute a base regen value: Willpower, intelligence or magicka.

Then a percent of this value is defined for the player and for other actors.

Finally, you can define the impact of multiple state-based factors:

[list]
[*]Willpower and intelligence are configured with percent ranges, defining the impact from the attribute level 0 to 100 (scaling continues above 100)[/*]
[*]Fatigue is configured with a percent range, defining the impact from 0 to full fatigue[/*]
[*]Encumbrance is configured with a percent range, defining the impact from a full capacity to no encumbrance[/*]
[*]Movement is configured with a percent applied when walking, and another percent applied when running[/*]
[*]Already regenerating actors (Restore Magicka effect) are configured with a percent applied during regen (100% by default)[/*]
[*]The Stunted Magicka effect is configured with a percent applied when such an effect is active on the actor (0% by default)[/*]
[*]Sleeping is configured with a percent applied when the player sleeps, in a bed or not (200% by default)[/*]
[/list]Over a long period of time (resting, waiting, traveling...), movement has no impact, fatigue only weighs while it comes back at its natural rate, and the magic effects that end during the period only count until they end.

[size=4]Load Order[/size]

Load order should not matter.

[size=4]Compatibility[/size]

[b]OpenMW 0.49 or above is required![/b]

Should be compatible with most mods.

May be compatible with other magicka regen mods, but it's obviously not advised.

[size=4]Performance[/size]

This mod has been designed from scratch for performance.
Current magicka value is checked for all active actors every second, not every frame.
Only actors who are not full of magicka get attached a script that will regenerate their magicka.
As soon as they are full of magicka again, the script is removed.
Also, when an actor becomes inactive, its script is removed, and the game time is saved in the global script to allow a proper magicka regeneration the next time this actor will be active.

[size=4]Installation[/size]

[list]
[*]Decompress the mod archive in a folder named, for instance, [font=Courier New]SBMR[/font][/*]
[*]In openmw.cfg

[list]
[*]Add the full path to the [font=Courier New]SBMR/00 Core[/font] directory as a data path[/*]
[*]Add [font=Courier New]state-based-magicka-regen.omwscripts[/font] as a content file[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]For example:

[code]data="C:\games\OpenMWMods\Gameplay\SBMR\00 Core"
content=state-based-magicka-regen.omwscripts[/code]
More info on how to install OpenMW mods [url=https://openmw.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/modding/mod-install.html]here[/url].

[size=3]Existing Games[/size]

It's safe to install or update this mod mid-game.

[size=3]Uninstallation[/size]

Just remove the mod files.

name: Rest and Sleep Recovery Options (OpenMW)
author: Dahatox
description: Choose which of the three resource stats to recover based on whether you are sleeping in a bed or resting.
usage_notes:
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/CBAElYb.png[/img]﻿

[b][color=#ff0000][size=4]Requires OpenMW[/size][/color]﻿﻿[/b][/center][b][size=4]Features:[/size][/b]
- The mod will simply try to restore the Health, Magicka and Fatigue to their previous values following a short delay after sleeping or resting. The delay is customizable.
- There are also separate options for portable beds like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45654]Frostwind[/url]'s Bedroll and Covered Bedroll (these 2 are added by default). So bringing a bed with you might not feel like cheating anymore.

[b][size=4]Known issues:[/size][/b]
- Resting near a bed counts as sleeping for the mod. So for example if you have Health recovery disabled for resting, but enabled for sleeping, then resting close to a bed will recover your health.
[b][color=#ff0000]!!! WARNING !!![/color][/b]
There might be unexpected events that cause the mod to fail, or even mess up your stats. If you find any problem, feel free to make a bug report or write a post, but don't expect me to fix it. Until it works reliably enough for me I won't bother fixing it.

name: Speechcraft Rebalance (OpenMW)
author: Aphain
description: Makes leveling speechcraft a better and worthwhile experience. Talk your way to the top!
usage_notes:
For [url=https://openmw.org/]OpenMW[/url]

This mod changes several game modifiers to make leveling speechcraft a more worthwhile and (hopefully) less broken experience.
It also dramatically increases the worth of speechcraft as a major or minor skill by nerfing "ye olde throw money at the problem" method.

Bribe modifers decreased to make bribes more reliant on mercantile and personality than
money to prevent rich characters with low social skills plowing through disposition checks.

[code]fBribe1000Mod 150 -> 125
fBribe100Mod 75 -> 45
fBribe10Mod 35 -> 20[/code]

Personality now has a slightly smaller influence on starting disposition (both positive and negative) 
to leave more room for speechcraft checks.

[code]fDispPersonalityMult 0,5 -> 0,35[/code]

Random dice rolls now have a lower impact on your speechcraft/mercantile checks.
This makes speechcraft/mercantile checks less random and more skill based.

[code]fPerDieRollMult 0,3 -> 0,2[/code]

Minimum success chance increased but minimum change per success decreased so that
leveling speechcraft is easier and has a greater longterm impact compared  to one or two
lucky rolls in a row in vanilla with huge disposition jumps. This also prevents low disposition
traps when you start out with a lower skill level.

[code]iPerMinChance 5 -> 30
iPerMinChange 10 -> 1[/code]

[b]Initial base disposition changes updated:[/b]

Attacking someone is now taken rather seriously by your victim...

[code]fDispAttacking -10 -> -25
[/code]
...and not so much anymore if they see you attacking somebody else.

[code]iDispAttackMod -50 -> -20[/code]

People don't like it when you start sneezing on their boots!

[code]fDispDiseaseMod -10 -> -15
[/code]
Increased same-race disposition bonus:

[code]fDispRaceMod 5 -> 10[/code]

People will now actually take it personally if they see you stealing (this is muliplied by stack value).

[code]fDispStealing -0,5 -> -1[/code]

Pickpocketing someone shouldn't be as bad as attacking them anymore...

[code]fDispPickPocketMod -25 -> -15[/code]

You want to taunt somebody? Draw your weapon before talking to them to lower their starting disposition!

[code]fDispWeaponDrawn -5 -> -10[/code]

Decreased disposition penalty for tresspassing (in vanilla tresspassing is equivalent to attacking two people!)

[code]iDispTresspass -20 -> -10[/code]

For an explanation about how social interactions work in the game see this page:
[url=https://wiki.openmw.org/index.php?title=Research:Disposition_and_Persuasion]Disposition and Personality Research[/url]

author: TipsyTechPriest
description:
Increases the Gold Value of Adamantium weapons to make more sense alongside Glass and Ebony.

They also now count as Silver Weapons, gaining the same magical 'purity' associated with silver. In game terms, they harm ghosts and are extra effective against Lycanthropes, giving them a special niche for Bloodmoon playthroughs.
usage_notes:
This mod increases the Gold Value of these weapons to give this neglected metal the justice it deserves! They also now count as Silver Weapons, gaining the same magical 'purity' associated with silver. In game terms, they harm ghosts and are extra effective against Lycanthropes, giving them a special niche for Bloodmoon playthroughs.

Some of the design choices made by the official DLCs are rather... questionable. The implementation of Adamantium weapons is one such case. In terms of damage and durability, they are placed a tier below Ebony. However, they are WAY too cheap for what you get. Let's compare:

...See what I mean? As implemented, Adamantium is dirt-cheap, but almost as good as Glass and Ebony! A relatively poor low- or mid-level character can buy them and easily become an early-game powerhouse, while they are almost worthless to a player looking to pawn off such powerful weapons.

name: Rafael's Shader Pack
author: Many people
description: Optimized postprocess shader pack for OpenMW, making it look better than ever before while still being very Vanilla-friendly
usage_notes:
[b][i]Shaders of light! Pixels of magic![/i]

[/b]A shader pack for OpenMW, using different shaders I've written or collected, tweaked, enhanced, fixed, optimized and changed in different ways, now in a single convenient place.
Enjoy a quality ambient occlusion to make the world look more grounded, quality anti-aliasing, enhanced lighting and weather effects to bring out the best out of Morrowind, while not changing the vanilla experience, and with a very small performance hit.
[b]
How to install the post process pack:[/b]
0. Make sure you have OpenMW (at least version 0.49)
1. Add RafaelsShaderPack to Data Directories in the launcher
2. Set OpenMW gamma to 1.0 and Minimum Interior Brightness to 0.00 (no need for such hacks since we're using tonemapping!), and ensure shaders are activated (if you use a higher view distance than 10 cells, I'd recommend going to 10, max. Reasoning is that shaders are tweaked for 2-10 cells, and lower view distances will also minimize any LOD or pop-in issues you'd encounter)
3. In-game, press F2 (you might need to enable postprocess from the in-game menu, in which case OpenMW tells you to do that), and move the following shaders from Inactive to Active in this order: [i]HBAO, VAIO, godrays, DIVE, wetworld, tonemap, SMAA [/i](or you can just copy and paste "chain = HBAO,VAIO,godrays,DIVE,wetworld,tonemap,SMAA" in the [Post Processing] section of your settings.cfg)
4. If you want temporal filtering (TAA minus temporal supersampling) or motion blur, then add SMB at the end. If not, skip it.
[b]
How to install the PBR lighting and filtered shadows shaders:[/b]
Check the installation instructions in each download.

[b]How to install the Various Data Enhancements:
[/b]Add as a normal mod, you can check or uncheck individual folders, and activate the related ESPs (if applicable). Core is related, the rest is up to you.

[b]Steps for performance boost:
[/b]Set the in-game water "reflection shader detail" to sky, and let the wetworld water SSR do the reflections instead. Considering this is anywhere between a 10% and 30% boost, it is beyond recommended.
If you're using a high shadow map resolution, it is also recommended to lower it, and to instead use the filtered shadows shaders. Too many users bump it to 4096 in order to get rid of ugly shadows when the actual solution isn't that.
If using a very high draw distance, then probably can be tuned a bit down. Anything higher than the game actually lets you is overkill, and usually leads to more aliasing, LOD issues, long loading times, hiccups, and so on. Nice for some screenshots, but not really for actual gameplay. And yes, other games can do this just fine, but different engines yield different results. 

[b]Performance knobs for shaders (if needed):[/b] 
1. Open the post process menu (F2), to go HBAO, and lower the exterior quality to any of the non-GTAO presets
2. If being near water is causing performance problems, then you can switch off the raymarched water by setting WATER_RAYMARCH_WAVES to 0 in lighting.glsl
3. If you notice a performance impact when using many parallax/height maps, then you can switch off the parallax shadows by setting PARALLAX_SHADOWS to 0 in lighting.glsl
 
[b]Quick guide to AA:[/b]
0. Best to use the enhanced PBR lighting shaders, as they have groundcover edge refinement (and some other tricks), thus severely reducing aliasing and shimmering caused by vegetation. The best anti-aliasing is not creating aliasing in the first place!
1. Ensure that SMAA is set to its default state, and change the resolve method to FXAA
2. If what aliasing you see is actual temporal instability or shimmering, but everything is fine when stationary, then what you need is SMB. The latest version also has a tweakable sharpness parameter, so you can find the sweet spot according to your own motion sensitivity
3. If you still somehow feel like there's not enough AA, then you can enable MSAA in the OMW launcher (called simply "Anti-aliasing"). Try 2x to begin with, it creates enough extra edge data in most cases
[b]Note that this can easily create problems between geometry and sky when using post process shaders. It is crucial that if you enable MSAA, then you also enable the sky rendering in VAIO, and you should also [url=https://pastebin.com/raw/cycxjedH]these[/url] in your openmw.cfg.
Note that adding more[i] post process AA[/i] will not lead "more" or better anti-aliasing! [/b]You're mostly just wasting performance. If AA was as easy as applying multiple types of [i]post processing AA[/i] on top of each other, I would've had an option for FXAA & SMAA together, yet I do not. Just like (almost) all games do not. While there might be some edge cases where doing this might look better, there's also cases where this [i]reintroduces[/i] aliasing.
4. If you want MSAA to also affect groundcover (and other transparent objects) then you need to enable "Use Anti-Aliased Alpha Testing" in the OMW launcher. Depending on your GPU and mods this can be a bit costly

Q&A
Q: My game looks very washed out now, why?
A: Ensure your gamma is set to 1.0. The HDR tonemapping and the other effects should lighten up dark areas enough by themselves. If you feel certain scenes are always too dark (for example not only [i]certain[/i] nights, but [i]all nights[/i]) then open up the tonemap settings (F2 -> tonemap, scroll down) and lower the Minimum Exposure (there's 3 of them, depending on your needs)

Q: But I always had gamma high when I played Morrowind, why change it now?
A: Because gamma is only on your monitor, it won't show up in captures, and it can mess up other stuff. Yes, I know that nowadays you can use a gamma or brightness post-process shader to do the same thing, but it's still better to get brighter colors through actual lighting and HDR correctness, which this shader pack is doing.

Q: How slow is my game going to run when using this?
A: The shaders included are optimized, making any performance hit barely noticeable. If someone can run OpenMW with its water shader enabled, then this pack should pose no problem at all.

Q: I use the same settings and a high resolution texture pack, and your screenshots still look more sharp than my game, why?
A: I also use normal maps as much as possible, and sometimes even specular or height maps. Those make a huge difference. Go download some, and enable the game to use them.

Q: When Android/Mac/MGE port?
A: Unsure. No promises.

Q: What about Steam Deck?
A: While I haven't tested it myself, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667?tab=posts&comment_id=162304987]this post[/url] covers installation.

Q: Anything I can do so torches and other lights don't constantly "flicker"?
A: This behaviour isn't from the shaders, it's tied to the lights themselves, so nothing I can do on my side. But, luckily, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55371]this mod[/url] updates them so they their radius is frozen in time.

Q: Any incompatibilities with other mods?
A: No, as far as I've tested. If you are using any other shader and/or post processing mods, make sure mine is loaded last so it can overwrite any old shaders. Exception are other modifications to the core OpenMW shaders! Do not try to mix and match, the optional files provided here are meant to be applied over default OpenMW shaders! Exception to the exception are mods that either clearly state compatibility, or are made specifically using these shaders as a base. Hope this isn't confusing!

Q: Any other incompatibilities?
A: There shouldn't be. But there could always be a weird combination of OpenMW version, operating system, graphics card and/or driver that can lead to either a shader not working at all or causing artifacts. If this happens to you, please post details (OMW version, graphics card used, in-game log with F10, how the problem can be reproduced, etc) and I will investigate.

name: Immersive Eyes-Body Reactions (OpenMW)
author: zenocite
description: OpenMW Immersive Eye/Blink, Yeah I know how this sounds. Blinking, in a video game? Feels like a joke mod at first glance, I get it. But give it a shot before you write it off. Once you've played with it a bit you actually start to notice when it's gone. Not just a cosmetic thing, it actually ties into gameplay too.
usage_notes:
[color=#f1c232][size=4][b]OpenMW Immersive Blink[/b][/size][/color]

Yeah I know how this sounds. Blinking, in a video game? Feels like a joke mod at first glance, I get it. But give it a shot before you write it off. Once you've played with it a bit you actually start to notice when it's gone. Just make sure to check all the extra features in the options!
The idea started with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/54864?tab=posts]Immersive Blinking[/url], full credit to the original creator for planting the seed. This is a full rebuild from scratch for OpenMW 0.51+ using native Lua, not just a cosmetic thing, it actually ties into gameplay too.

[color=#f1c232][size=4][b]Reactive mode[/b][/size][/color] is worth calling out specifically, since it changes what blinking actually is in the mod. By default your character blinks naturally on their own the whole time, ambient and constant. Switch to Reactive mode instead and that idle blinking turns off completely, blinking only happens when it actually means something, getting genuinely exhausted, staring into a storm, clearing the blur after surfacing from water. It turns blinking into a real feedback loop instead of background flavor, a way of reading your character's actual state without opening a menu.

[img width=418]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788054030-52117301.gif[/img][img width=420]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788125538-605291720.gif[/img]
[heading][color=#f1c232]What it does[/color][/heading]
Your character blinks on its own, randomized so it doesn't feel robotic. You can tune the timing however you want in the settings menu, remap the manual blink key through the normal controls menu, and set your own eyes-closed color, grey and black options both available.
It also reacts to stuff around you features down below!

[heading][color=#b45f06]Optional: Super Settings Renderers[/color][/heading]
[b][color=#f1c232]Super Settings Renderers[/color][/b] ([url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59673]https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59673[/url]) - not required, but cleans up the settings menu a lot. Sliders instead of typing numbers into boxes, easier to adjust, way less bloated looking overall. Works fine without it too, everything just falls back to the normal controls.

[size=4][b]Also check out my other mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/60121]Openmw Personality![/url][/b][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788409443-1610818960.gif[/img]

[b][u][color=#f1c232]What's new in 0.4.0![/color][/u][/b]

[list]
[*][color=#ffd966]Storm reactions[/color] ash storms, blight storms, blizzards, and heavy rain now make your character shield their eyes if you're facing into the wind, same idea as the sun squint, complete with objects correctly blocking it[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]A quick flutter-blink[/color] when facing into wind during a storm without your hand raised[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]A manual hotkey[/color] for the hand-raise gesture tap it to trigger yourself, hold it to shut the whole system off when you want a break from it[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Underwater blur [/color]now has two modes the original build-up-over-time version, or a steady constant blur that works completely independently of blinking[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]A softer[/color] more gradual blink style, available as an alternative to the original[/*]
[/list][img width=428]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788317155-1129861430.gif[/img][img width=428]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788317617-553365771.gif[/img]

[b]If you're updating from an older version, make sure to try out the new soft blink as the updated default way to experience blinking.[/b]

[list]
[*][color=#ffd966]Moving between cells [/color]including a little flicker when you step from a dark interior out into daylight[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Weather[/color] certain types will make you blink more, and you can customize which ones[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Coming up out of water[/color] you won't blink underwater but you'll get a few quick blinks right as you surface, like you're clearing water out of your eyes[/*]
[*][color=#b45f06]Optional[/color], more frequent blinking while submerged, your eyes irritated from the water[/*]
[*][color=#b45f06]Optional[/color], a screen blur that builds the longer you go without blinking underwater, clears instantly on any blink[/*]
[*][color=#b45f06]Optional[/color], a licensed face wipe animation plays when you come up out of the water instead of or alongside the surfacing blinks, skips itself if you've got a weapon or spell readied[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Low health[/color] once you drop below a threshold you'll start blinking more too[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Waking up from sleep[/color] your vision fades in gradually instead of snapping clear, with a couple quick blinks to finish clearing it[/*]
[*][color=#ffd966]Added an optional sun squint[/color] Look at the sun outdoors for a bit and your character raises a hand to shield their eyes. Drops back down when you look away, when something blocks the sun, after a max hold time, or if you draw a weapon or ready a spell. Fully configurable timing, off by default[/*]
[*][color=#b45f06]Pretty much everything here has its own setting [/color][/*]
[/list][img width=428]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788149460-1923685973.gif[/img][img width=428]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788055459-1893204135.gif[/img]
[heading][color=#38761d]Works with other mods[/color][/heading]
This one's grown into a bit of a collaboration between a few different mod authors, all optional, all read only, none of it changes the mods being integrated with.

[b][color=#38761d]Sun's Dusk Needs and Survival[/color][/b] - blinking ties directly into your exhaustion level, the more worn out you get the more you'll blink, plus an optional slower blur that builds as fatigue sets in.

[b][color=#38761d]Devilish Alcohol Overhaul[/color] (latest version required)[/b] - blink rate follows your actual drunk state, getting heavy and droopy the more intoxicated you get, with some stumbling once you're deep into it.

[b][color=#38761d]Devilish Touch of Madness[/color] (latest version required)[/b] - blinking scales across five stages of a skooma trip, quicker and more erratic the higher it climbs.

[b][color=#38761d]Praying Animated[/color][/b] - your eyes squint while the prayer animation is actually playing. Soft letterbox, strongest at the top and bottom of the screen, clear through the middle so you can still see your hands.

[b][color=#1155cc]Face wipe/thumbs down animation[/color][/b] - licensed from Dubiousnpc, bundled into this mod with permission.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788078266-167299074.gif[/img]
(Slight incremental blur tied to your Sun Dusk sleep bar cleared with blinks, chance for micro sleep events)
[heading][color=#7f6000]Tomb Respect[/color][/heading]
A gameplay feature, optional and kind of a roleplay thing:

[list]
[*]In ancestral tombs, Ancestor Ghosts, Skeletons, and Bonewalkers won't attack you on sight as long as your eyes are closed, like you're paying respect to the dead[/*]
[*]Keeping your eyes open is totally fine too, it's just if you stare directly at one for too long (4 seconds by default, adjustable) it takes that as a challenge and attacks[/*]
[*]Closing your eyes resets the stare timer, so you can look away and reset if you need to[/*]
[*]Loot anything in the tomb though and it alerts everything in there straight to your position, so it's not a free pass, you still gotta fight for your loot if you want it[/*]
[/list]Everything above can be toggled on or off separately in the settings.

[img width=803]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/60045/60045-1788056325-1383719837.gif[/img]

[heading][color=#900000]Requirements[/color][/heading]
OpenMW 0.51 or newer.
If you want the face wipe animation to actually show up, turn on "Use additional animation sources" in the OpenMW Launcher, under Visuals then Animations.
[list]
[*]1. Download and extract the archive to a folder you'll remember. It doesn't need to go inside your Morrowind install, OpenMW can load mods from anywhere. [/*]
[*]2. Open the OpenMW Launcher and go to the Data Files tab. [/*]
[*]3. Add the extracted folder as a data directory (there's an Append/Add button, or you can drag the folder into the list). [/*]
[*]4. In the Content Files list further down, find this mod's .omwscripts file and make sure the checkbox next to it is ticked. This step is easy to miss and if it's not checked the mod will just silently do nothing. [/*]
[*]5. Launch the game. Settings for this mod appear under Options in the scripts section.[/*]
[/list][heading]Open for ideas[/heading]
Bug reports and suggestions are genuinely wanted. Also open to integration ideas or collab suggestions if you think something would pair well with this.

If you like this one, you might enjoy my other OpenMW mods:

name: Rock The Boat - Dynamic Camera Rocking for OpenMW
author: Leaposter
description: Enables dynamic camera rocking when standing on a boat or rope bridge, and while water walking or swimming.
usage_notes:
[b]Description:[/b]
Rock The Boat is a mod that enables dynamic camera rocking when standing on a boat, in a boat interior, on a rope bridge, while water walking, and/or while swimming.

Not required, but the effect looks and works best when installed along side [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] and the enhanced water shader with raymarched waves from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667]Rafael's Shader Pack[/url].

[b]Features & Functionality:[/b]
[list]
[*]Rocking is directional, based on the player's orientation relative to the boat or bridge.[/*]
[*]Rocking intensity is configurable per-weather-type.[/*]
[*]Rocking can be enabled or disabled for interiors and exteriors independently of one another. [/*]
[*]Rocking can be enabled or disabled for boats, bridges, water walking, and swimming independently of one another.[/*]
[*]There is an "Anti-Nausea" toggle for those sensitive to the rocking motion, which will replace camera roll with camera pitch. [/*]
[/list]
[b]Compatibility:[/b]
Unlike other mods which attempt to animate the boats themselves, this only animates the camera, making it compatible with any and all existing boat mods. If you encounter a boat that should be rocking that isn't, or a boat that rocks on the wrong axis, or a boat that shouldn't be rocking that is, please feel free to report the issue (with the object name) so it can be profiled!

Rock the Boat is fully compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] as of v0.5. Ensure that Rock the Boat is loaded [i]after[/i] Dynamic Camera. Installing Dynamic Camera will further improve interoperability with other mods that alter the camera using its framework.

[b]Recommended Mods:[/b]
A selection of mods that I find pair nicely with Rock The Boat.
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/55327]Dynamic Camera[/url] - Rock the Boat will use Dynamic Camera for camera control, if present.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53667]Rafael's Shader Pack[/url] - Rock the Boat was made with Raf's enhanced water shader's raymarched waves in mind.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53637]Red Mountain Tremors[/url] - For even more camera-shaking fun![/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58443]Animated Lanterns and Signs[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/49767]Morrowind Animated Hammocks[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59393]Arrive Whenever[/url] - Shameless self plug, but Morrowind [i]does[/i] start on a boat![/*]
[/list]

name: Can't Touch This - Combat Miss Feedback (OpenMW)
author: MrArrean and Dubiousnpc
description: Adds "dodge" animations to NPCs that you've attacked but missed. Creating a layer of visual feedback in additional to aural "whoosh" that vanilla Morrowind offers. Currently only Humanoid NPCs are covered.
usage_notes:
[b][size=4]# Can't Touch This: OpenMW Lua Combat Feedback [/size][/b]

This is "miss feedback" feature of [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58658]N'Garde[/url][/b] extracted for people that prefer vanilla combat and/or don't care about the parry/active block.

Do not use both mods at the same time, N'Garde fully incorporates everything this mod possibly has to offer.

[b][size=4]# Why does this exist?[/size]
[/b][size=3]Because lack of combat feedback from enemy actors is [i][b][u]the #1[/u][/b][/i] most common complaint about Morrowind combat.

But, I like vanilla hit-chance mechanics - they offer another balance lever to developers to tune combat, and hence save Morrowind from the wet-noodle-weapon syndrome of later TES games.

Why was this separated from the main mod? Because I acknowledge that there are players out there that do not want to mess with parrying, active blocking and anything that entails. 

Adding a setting to the mod that would disable core functionality seemed silly. Hence this. 

At this time mod includes 11 miss-dodge "bob and weave" animations that will play when your attack misses on a Humanoid Target.

Range of actors covered may be expanded in the future.

Again - use one or the other. One day I may revisit this and interop them a bit, so I don't have to duplicate the code, but that day is not today. If you already have N'Garde installed - move along. If you don't because you dislike what its core has to offer - this one is for you.
Hope you enjoy.[/size]

[size=4][b]# Installation:[/b][/size]
- Place the unpacked directory in a convenient location.
- Add the path to the uncompressed directory in OpenMW launcher "Data Directories" tab
- Enable provided canttouchthis.omwscripts file
- Enable "Use Additional Animation Sources" setting in the launcher
- Enable "smooth animation transitions" setting in the launcher
- Enable "smooth movement" setting in the launcher. 

[size=4][b]# Compatibility:[/b][/size]
[size=3]Should be compatible with anything and everything. Except the parent mod. Again, use one or the other.[/size]

[size=4][b]# Credits:[/b]
[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/Dubiousnpc]Dubiousnpc[/url] - 8 of 11 miss-dodge animations. [/b][/size]

name: Over-the-Shoulder Combat Stance (OpenMW Camera script edit)
author: Ctroost
description: Edit of the OpenMW third-person camera script that allows the player to retain the over-the-shoulder view when entering the combat stance, because I found the switch to a centered view very disorienting.
usage_notes:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]This mod allows the OpenMW's third-person camera behavior to be changed so that the over-the-shoulder view is retained when entering the combat stance, instead of snapping to a centered view. The default centered switch can feel a little disorienting mid-fight.[/color]

This is a very simple edit of the [i][b]third_person.lua[/b][/i] script found in [b][i]resources\vfs\scripts\omw\camera[/i][/b] in your OpenMW installation folder. 

If you would like to manually edit the script yourself, remove the following line:
[code]if Actor.getStance(self) ~= Actor.STANCE.Nothing and mode == MODE.ThirdPerson then state = STATE.Combat [/code]
Then change this line:
[code]elseif Actor.isSwimming(self) then state = STATE.Swimming [/code]
to:
[code]if Actor.isSwimming(self) then state = STATE.Swimming [/code]
Save the file and enjoy.

[u]An improved version of the mod was provided by Jazilla, allowing for the enabling or disabling of the over-the-shoulder combat stance at will through the in-game OpenMW Camera script.[/u]
[line]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]
Install like any other mod through the OpenMW launcher. 

Alternatively, if you're using the original version of the mod, you can drop the resources folder into your OpenMW installation folder, or drop the edited third_person.lua file into resources\vfs\scripts\omw\camera. Overwrite the existing file, and you're done.
[line]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW (I haven't tested the edited Lua file on any other versions besides 0.51.0, but it would probably work fine unless changes have been made to the script since older OpenMW versions.)[/color]
[line]
[size=4][b]Credits[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]OpenMW team for the original script.
Jazilla for providing an improved version of the mod.[/color]

name: TimeHUD - A Clock UI widget

[color=#9fc5e8][size=3]features[/size]
[/color]- easily move the widget by clicking and dragging, lock in place
- change color using a full color picker with presets

name: Best Friends Forever (OpenMW)
author: SosnoviyBor
description: A collection of utilities for followers made with performance in mind. Follower HUD, teleportation, immortality and more. Modernized Attend Me, if you will.
usage_notes:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51232]Attend Me[/url] is great, but it can be improved. That's why I'm presenting to you Best Friends Forever - performant and modernized alternative to Attend Me with extra flair!

[b][color=#b6d7a8][size=4]Features[/size][/color][/b]
Note that effectively everything in this mod toggleable and configurable.

[b][color=#a4c2f4][size=4]Follower HUD[/size][/color][/b]
Convenient way to see you followers' status.
[list]
[*]Current and total health, magicka and fatigue[/*]
[*]Equipped weapon, spell, disease or the lack of them[/*]
[/list][b][color=#a4c2f4][size=4]Teleportation Module[/size][/color][/b]
You will never lose your followers again. Everywhere you go - they will be teleported to you, including:
[list]
[*]Cell transitions[/*]
[*]Recall and intervention[/*]
[*]Travel services[/*]
[*]Scripted teleports[/*]
[/list][quote]Note: this module might break certain scripted events like follower departure. If you encounter this, use script blacklist and let me know about the issue somewhere so I could add a rule to the default config.[/quote]
[b][color=#a4c2f4][size=4]Catch Up Module[/size][/color][/b]
Younger brother to Teleportation. Simply put, your followers will speed up the further they get from you. Meaning they will keep up with you even without needing to wear the Boots of Blinding Speed.

[b][color=#a4c2f4][size=4]Immortality Module[/size][/color][/b]
Ever been annoyed that your story-rich follower constantly dies in combat, borking the questline and requiring you to reload the save? Yeah, I did too. Well, you will never lose your followers again. Again.

This module will make sure your followers won't ever get killed pernanently. Instead, they will fall on the ground for set amount of time or until the end of the combat. Additionally, all enemies will ignore them lying on the ground, keeping the difficulty mostly in tact.
Does not apply to:
[list]
[*]Summons[/*]
[*]Actors under any Command effect[/*]
[/list][quote]Note: this module might break scripted events when your followers have to engage in combat with you. The solution is the same as with TP module.[/quote]
[color=#a4c2f4][size=4][b]Ward Module[/b][/size][/color]
Module to remove one more friction point in playing with followers. Ward will protect your followers from all diseases and stat damage.

Disabled by default.

[b][color=#a4c2f4][size=4]Call Keybind[/size][/color][/b]
A keybing to unstuck your followers. Teleport everyone to you at the press of a button.

Unbound by default.

[b][color=#b6d7a8][size=4]Compatibility[/size][/color][/b]
Safe to install or update mid-playthrough.
When removing the mod, make sure no follower is currently downed and they don't have a speed boost.

Should be compatible with anything.
It is technically compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51232]Attend Me[/url], but they should not be used together.

Supported edge case mods:
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58901]Loafy's Necromancy - Reanimate Dead[/url] by TheLoafyOne[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/42417]Water Life[/url] by abot[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/46538]Inquisitive Guards[/url] by RubberMan[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/6006]Morrowind Comes Alive[/url] by Neoptolemus and Morrowind community[/*]
[/list][color=#b6d7a8][size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size][/color]
Load BFF as high as possible in the load order - before any mods that might alter melee damage calculations.
[list]
[*]OpenMW 0.52 or newer[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58053]Follower Detection Util[/url] version 3.1 or newer - Load before BFF[/*]
[/list][b][color=#b6d7a8][size=4]Recommended Mods[/size][/color][/b]
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57975]Friendlier Fire[/url][/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/58818]Follower Commands[/url][/*]
[/list][b][color=#b6d7a8][size=4]API[/size][/color][/b]
Events:
[code]-- Sent when the player clicks certain follower's widget
-- Payload: Actor (follower object)
-- Scope: Player, Global
BestFriendsForever_followerWidgetClicked

-- Sent when the follower enters Downed state
-- Payload: { follower: Actor, leader: Actor }
-- Scope: Player, Global
BestFriendsForever_followerDown

-- Sent when the follower is released from the Downed state
-- Payload: { follower: Actor, leader: Actor }
BestFriendsForever_followerUp[/code]Interfaces:
[code]-- Returns downed followers of the player
-- Returns: table<string, Actor>
-- Scope: Player
I.BestFriendsForever.getDownedFollowers()[/code]

[size=5][b]⊹ How To Remove Vanilla Enemy Health Bar[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Find [font=Courier New]./OpenMW/resources/vfs/mygui/openmw_hud.layout[/font] (inside your OpenMW folder, not your Morrowind folder!), if you are using a mod replacing/modifying vanilla hud, such as the beautiful [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53267?tab=posts&BH=1]Centered HUD for OpenMW[/url] - look for [font=Courier New]/mygui/openmw_hud.layout[/font] inside the mod folder instead (if you are using a mod manager to install it)[/*]

[/list]
e.g you might find an element that looks like this

[code]<Widget type="ProgressBar" skin="MW_EnergyBar_Yellow" position="0 131 80 12" align="Center Bottom" name="EnemyHealth">
    <Property key="Visible" value="false"/>
</Widget>[/code]
inside position = "..." change 80 to 0. Save the file. Play the game.
