[center][u][b]Under Construction [/b][/u][/center]
 
[b]Summary [/b]
 
With this mod, construction materials and scaffolding will be visible at the Great House strongholds during construction of the later stages.
 
[b]Description [/b]
 
It's commonly understood that the Great House strongholds have three stages, but they actually have six phases. In addition to the three main stages, there are also three intermediate phases during which various portions of the stronghold are under construction. Bethesda implemented the first intermediate phase (where the first stage of the stronghold is under construction), but did not fully implement the other two (where the second and third stages are in progress).
 
The developers went to the trouble of creating the required objects (scaffolding, wood planks, buckets, and so on) and placing them in the world, as well as assigning them scripts to ensure they'll only be visible during the appropriate construction phases. However, they just never actually set the relevant global variable to the proper values to implement these later intermediate phases.
 
When construction first begins on your stronghold, the main building is inaccessible, and you'll see various construction materials nearby. But, in the vanilla game, due to Bethesda's partial implementation, there are no such intermediate phases later on. When construction of the second stage of the stronghold begins, there are no changes at the stronghold at all; when construction is complete, the new buildings pop into existence fully built. The same thing happens with the third stage.
 
This mod finishes the job that Bethesda started by implementing the last two intermediate phases. Now, when construction of the second or third stage of your stronghold begins, you can visit the stronghold and actually see the new buildings - inaccessible, for now - in progress, along with scaffolding and assorted construction materials lying about. The site foremen are also active during the intermediate phases.
 
After the requisite amount of time has passed, the under construction phase will be complete, the construction materials will be gone, and the new buildings will be accessible.
 
The mod also fixes a couple errors in the vanilla Raven Rock scripts (principally one that caused certain objects to be disabled when they shouldn't be), but does not otherwise touch Raven Rock.
 
[b]Installation [/b]
 
Use a mod management tool such as [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/45439]Wrye Mash[/url], or just copy the plugin to your Data Files directory and select it in the Morrowind Launcher.
 
[b]Compatibility [/b]
 
This mod edits the following vanilla scripts:
 
Strong_Build2_H
Strong_Build2_R
Strong_Build2_T
Strong_Build3_H
Strong_Build3_R
Strong_Build3_T
Strong3_Not
ColonyFactor3_D
Colony_E_Torch
 
It will be incompatible (without a patch at least) with any mod that touches the Strong_Build scripts. Stronghold overhauls should be okay, but any mod that changes the actual process of stronghold construction might touch the scripts.
 
I'm not aware of any other mods that edit the Strong3_Not script, but if one does, the conflict will be relatively minor - certain parts of Tel Uvirith that shouldn't be accessible until stage 3 is complete might be accessible during the under construction phase for stage 3.

Regarding the two Raven Rock (colony) scripts, if any other mod touches those scripts, it should come after this one in your load order.
 
The above script edits represent most of this mod's changes, although a couple manual adjustments to Tel Uvirith were necessary in order to prevent reaching certain areas before they're supposed to be accessible. The only actual cell edit is to the exterior cell Uvirith's Grave: placing two unopenable doors that will only be visible during the intermediate phase for stage 3. If you're using a mod that changes the exterior placement of Omavel's or Seleth's houses, this might result in a little weirdness. The other Tel Uvirith-related edits *shouldn't* result in conflicts, but I'm not 100% certain about that.
 
[b]Version History [/b]
 
Version 1.1 - 2021-10-05
   - Fixed a couple errors in the vanilla Raven Rock scripts, principally one that caused certain trees/rocks at the SE factor's estate location to be disabled when they shouldn't be.
   - Raven Rock is otherwise untouched.

Version 1.0 - 2021-09-29
   - Initial release.
 
[b]Contact [/b]
 
Feel free to contact me on the Nexus with any comments or suggestions. You can also find me on Discord as Necrolesian#9692.
 
[b]Usage [/b]
 
You can use this however you want.

name: Dubdilla Location Fix
author: Half11
description: This mod fixes another one of Beth's oversights. One of MW's quests has voiced dialogue that sends you to a totally different location than where the quest actually takes place. I just put the cave entrance in a more logical location.
usage_notes:
[size=3]
[/size][center][size=3][u][img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/565349428760805376/578562858686611456/H2PxwN2.png[/img][/u]

[img]data:image/png;base64,[/img]

One of MW's quests has voiced dialogue that sends you to a totally different location than where the quest actually takes place (and completely contradicts the journal, for that matter). Without a bag of money, it is not easy to hire Wes Johnson (the voice actor) to rectify this. Redoing the voice by someone else would be lame, right?

So I just put the cave entrance in a more logical location; so that this glaring and immersion-breaking inconsistency is fixed.
• Directions in the journal now correspond to the dialogue.
• Mount Assarnibibi will be marked on your map as soon as the quest begins.
• Removed any sign of the previous entrance in the Grazelands.
• No landscape edits were made.

[b][color=#ff0000]*SPOILER ALERT*[/color][/b]
When doing the "A Cure for Vampirism" quest for Molag Bal, his dialogue says that Molag Grunda is found in the caverns of Dubdilla under Mount Assernibibi. But the caverns are near Vos, and the journal tells you it is south of Vos. It does make sense that the cave Dubdilla is located below Mount Assarnibibi. According to Temple lore, this is where Molag Bal oversaw the 99 lovers of Boethiah, who gave birth to Almalexia. So there is a connection.

name: Cavern Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Overhaul of almost all the caves on Vvardenfell utilizing Tamriel_Data.
usage_notes:
The overhauls this mod makes range from minor to medium. Fundamentally, these are still vanilla caves, preserving the thought put into them by Bethesda devs who designed them. 


All caves that are listed on [url=https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Morrowind:Caves]this[/url] page were modified, with the exception of the Sixth House bases, the Corprusarium, Cavern of the Incarnate, Tukushapal and Urshilaku Burial Caverns. This mod also incorporates all the previous overhauls that I made and improves upon them, except for Sargon and Mount Kand, Cavern, which were remade from scratch for this mod.


Several things were done to improve the user experience:

1. Cluttering and detailing: no all-rockers, no rock spam that entirely covers the cave walls. I was going off of vanilla rock placements, and never strayed too far away from how it does certain things. Not a single cave exceeds 600 refs, so you can be sure that the cells this mod touches will not start lagging after you install this mod.
Cluttering was done where it made sense, whether it's beverages the bandits are drinking, or a set of Hortator cards/dices that they entertain themselves with.

2. Lighting: all new and modified vanilla light source placements are made to account for greenlighting and the 8-light-source-per-mesh Morrowind.exe limit (read more on greenlight [url=https://wiki.project-tamriel.com/wiki/Interior_Guidelines#Greenlight]here[/url]). That means that all of the 400 radius tikitorches were thrown out of the window, and replaced with 256/177/128 radius variants. While that helps with issues such a light leaks, some users may perceive the caves to be darker than before. Unfortunately, there is nothing that can be done with that, as this is how the vanilla engine handles lighting, and I wanted to give vanilla Morrowind.exe players a pleasant experience too alongside the per-pixel lighting users.
Aside from light source placements, all ambient and sunlight lighting values were standardized. Sunlight values are 10/10/10 for all cells, and ambient lighting is increased and given a color based on the cave type. For mold caves I went with a mix of blue/green, mud caves are red/green to give off a yellow-ish hue, lava caves are given a red hue, mage caves (which have at least a single crystal placed) are given a blue-ish hue, and daedra-related caverns such as Kora-Dur and Dubdilla (the uncharted caverns part) were given a red/blue mix. It should be noted that there are exceptions to these standards.

3. Floaters, bleeders, caspers misplaced/misaligned objects: I thoroughly checked for any of the aforementioned issues that were present in vanilla caves, and tried my best to fix them. There are probably hundreds of fixes made by this mod.

4. Pathgrids: redone for every single cell this mod touches. While I can't claim that I'm experienced in pathgridding and know all the tricks, I tested every single cave in Morrowind.exe and can confirm that enemies navigate properly in and out of combat. OpenMW users should has even less issues with enemy AI. This also brings fixes by itself, too, such as unconnected nodes/underwater nodes being deleted.


Compatibility: incompatible with all mods that overhaul the locations this mod touches. The only compatible mods are those that create a whole other shell in the same cell and place the player there, leaving the original dungeon intact. I don't know about any mods which may place new quest items in cells that may conflict with this mod's placements, so please report those and I'll make a patch for them if I can. Lighting mods (Necro's TLAD, di.Still.ed Lights) should generally be fine to place above my mod, as the WGHT records weren't touched. Although I'm aware that TLAD makes edits to some cells so please report those incompatibilities too.


Due to the sheer amount of work poured into this mod, expect bugs and glitches. Don't forget to report them too.


The screenshots on the mod page may not correspond to individual user experience. I use OpenMW with core shader replacements and post-processing shaders.


Mod cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes.

author: Kramn1k
description: Minor overhaul of the Tukushapal burial cavern.
usage_notes:
As stated, the changes this mod makes are minimal. It's probably hard to even call it an overhaul. Still, I consider it an improvement over the original. 


As usual in my refit series, I fixed all the floaters/bleeders I could find, eliminated all instances of greenlight, edited pathgrids and edited the "Tukushapal" cell lighting settings to be less grey. The biggest amount of work in this mod is probably deleting all the internal geometry that was hidden behind the rocks. The developer probably initially made the shell with velothi pieces, then added rocks everywhere and forgot to clean up afterwards. I don't think this will actually bring a performance improvement but it's still a worthy change imo.


Compatibility: should be compatible with pretty much anything. 


Cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes.

name: Mine Refit
author: Kramn1k
description: Overhaul of all the mines on Vvardenfell utilizing Tamriel_Data.
usage_notes:
This mod does several notable things, aside from the usual bugfixing, lighting and pathgrid improvements I make in my refit series. 

1. Quarters for miners! Yes, finally, all the FUNCTIONING mines have miner quarters. Did you ever notice that the vanilla mines were lacking that? Personally, I haven't. I don't think a lot of people care enough. I mainly added them because PTR does so, and I want this mod to be up to the project's standard. 

2. Utilizing TD kwama assets in egg mines.
TD introduces several new cool looking kwama assets that help diversify the egg mines which previously only had kwama eggs to somehow distinct themselves from other mines/caves, and this mod spreads them across all the egg mines. The care I put into the placement of these assets is magnitudes better than my old egg mine mod, which I'll still leave up for anyone who wants to download it, but under no circumstances do I recommend doing so. 

3. Adding new egg miners.
In several vanilla egg mines you could see NPCs named "Egg Miner", which is quite weird for MW which usually properly names all NPCs except guards. I added new records with properly named Egg Miners and changed their loot tables to give them egg miner hooks (new TD asset), new faces/hair and partially dressed them in TD clothing. This is probably the most compatibility problematic change this mod does, since some mods may use the vanilla records for quests. Please report such compatibility issues and I'll see what I can do.

For other stuff this mod does, consult [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/57827]Cavern Refit's[/url]﻿ page description which gives a more in-depth explanation on what else you can expect from this modification.



Compatibility: incompatible with any mod that overhauls mines. I edited WGHT records in certain cells which will create incompatibilities with mods such as TLAD or di.still.ed Lights, so please place them above my mod in your load order.


Due to the amount of work poured into this mod, expect bugs and glitches. Don't forget to report them too.

post-processing shaders.


Mod cleaned with TESAME and TES3CMD. Credits to Assumeru (and other code contributors) for the [url=https://github.com/TD-Addon/StandardsValidator]StandardsValidator[/url] tool which helped me spot any unconnected/underwater pathgrid nodes.

name: Vanilla Morrowind Trees - Animated
author: Silrorj and MOP team
description: Gives wind animations to the vanilla trees of Morrowind, Tribunal and Bloodmoon, based on the Morrowind Optimization Patch meshes.
usage_notes:
This mod adds a gentle wind animation to the vanilla trees of Morrowind, Tribunal and Bloodmoon. Leaves sway softly while trunks stay still, so the landscape feels a bit more alive without changing the look of the original trees.


It covers the trees of the Ascadian Isles, the Grazelands, the West Gash, the Bitter Coast (leaves and hanging moss), Mournhold and Solstheim (including the snowy pines), as well as a few small bushes. Dead and leafless trees are left untouched.


The meshes are based on the Morrowind Optimization Patch, so you keep all of its fixes and optimizations. MOP is not required, but if you use it, load this mod after it. 

Tree replacers that use the same meshes will override this mod for those trees, depending on your load order.

The performance impact is minimal, since only a few extra parts per tree are animated.


Credits go to the MOP team for the Morrowind Optimization Patch meshes, and to Vurt, whose animated trees inspired this mod

usage_notes:
Adds gentle, subtle leaf sway to over 400 trees from Tamriel Data, covering Tamriel Rebuilt, Project Cyrodiil, Skyrim Home of the Nords and the other projects using it.


The foliage of each tree sways softly on its own loop, while trunks and collision stay static. Tall, narrow trees such as poplars and cone spruces sway gently as a whole from their base. 

Geometry, UVs and textures are identical to the original. Bare trees, trees that are already animated in Tamriel Data and underwater kelp trees are left untouched. 

Performance cost should be minimal.
This mod also fixes the flickering leaves on the Cyrodiil poplar, which were caused by overlapping leaves in the original model.
You need the original mod: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/44537]Tamriel Data[/url]
Install after it and let this mod overwrite the meshes.


[u][b]Credits[/b][/u]: the Tamriel Data team and all the artists who created those trees, and Vurt for the animation method used in his Animated Solstheim Trees.

author: RandomPal
description: Adds a windmill to the Arano Plantation
usage_notes:
This mod adds an animated windmill to the Arano Plantation.

[b]Why the Arano Plantation?[/b]

Simply put: aesthetics. The windmill model, sourced from TR_data, is beautifully crafted but notably large and visually prominent. Because windmills need to be positioned on reasonably elevated ground, I found that suitable spots for such a feature were actually quite limited without requiring major landscape adjustments—something not warranted for a small addition like this.

While a minor addition, it should help enhance the atmosphere of the plantations overall.

I hope you like the mod! Cheers!

name: More Indoril Indoril Settlements
author: Damius
description: Updates Akamora, Ammar, Nan Iban, and Enamor Dayn to the newer Indoril tileset.
usage_notes:
[u][b]Summary[/b][/u]

When Poison Song released with its new Indoril tileset for Roa Dyr and talk of removing all the Mournhold architecture I was expecting the older Sacred East era Indoril settlements to have been updated too. I found out those have been shelved for a future full rework and rewrite potentially a few years out so for now we have a very stark divide between old and new content. 

I'm not patient enough for that so I’m updating them myself to the new tileset while keeping as close as possible to the original layout and intent. Some details had to be rearranged, like windows or entrances to diagonal buildings that don't have equivalents in the new tileset. [i]Most [/i]of the interiors are one for one swaps to their nearest equivalent parts, but the manors of the quest/plot related noble families were all remade to be chapel-manors. 

I also trimmed down the mountains and rocks around Akamora significantly, my fps went up for 30ish to about 60. There was quite a few rocks that were outright buried in a way that the player could never see, and a fair few that were massive but only the barest top was exposed so nothing significant was lost with their removal. This has also spilled out to some cells surrounding Akamora but not as heavily.

Note that I’m using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/59978]my Indoril retexture[/url] in the screenshots.

[b][u]Planned[/u][/b]

My current plan is to work down the settlements that have quests first, then any that are likely to be visible going to or looking from quest related areas, then clean up of the remaining monasteries, plantations, and farms after.

[s]Enamor Dayn[/s] - Complete

description: The Concept Art Palace mod (C.A.P.) is my attempt to bring the Vivec palace closer the original Kirkbride's concept art.The palace is now back to be worthy of God.
usage_notes:
[center]﻿[/center]
[center]﻿[/center]
[center][/center]
[center]﻿
[img]https://agrabush.com/inom-media/part-of-modathon-2020.png[/img][/center]
[b]Concept Art Palace (C.A.P.)[/b]

[i]Introduction:[/i]
The Concept Art Palace mod (C.A.P.) aims to bring the Vivec palace closer to Michael Kirkbride's original concept art, restoring its divine grandeur. This mod transforms the palace into a structure worthy of divine presence.

[b]Contents:[/b]
I. Requirements
II. Description
III. Compatibility
IV. Installation and Removal
V. Credits and Permissions
VI. Suggested Mods

[b]I. Requirements:[/b]
[list]
[*]Morrowind[/*]
[*]Tribunal[/*]
[*]Bloodmoon[/*]
[*]Tamriel_Data[/*]
[*]OAAB_Data[/*]
[/list][b]II. Description:[/b]
In stark contrast to the vanilla dome's simplicity, the palace concept art depicts a majestic sight: a blazing green fire surrounded by eight
revolving planets, constructed from bronze, glass, and opal. This installation is fully customizable via a FOMOD-BAIN installer, providing
pictures, descriptions, and instructions for installing the various options. Take your time to read them properly.

[i]The 3 main versions are:
[/i]
A symmetric palace, with 3 set of stairs and 4 chapels dedicated to praise Vivec.
An Asymmetric palace with 2 set of stairs and 2 chapels that functions as Vivec's chambers.
An untouched version which leave the Palace exterior untouched.

Following this design as closely as possible, CAP main version includes the following folders:

[u]    00 Core[/u]
        meshes: Contains mesh files necessary for the mod.
        textures: Contains texture files necessary for the mod.

[u]    01 Symmetrical Palace[/u]
        meshes: Contains mesh files specific to the symmetrical palace design.
        Concept art palace.ESP: Plugin file for the symmetrical palace design.

[u]    01 Asymmetrical Palace[/u]
        meshes: Contains mesh files specific to the asymmetrical palace design.
        Concept art palace.ESP: Plugin file for the asymmetrical palace design.

[u]    02 Interior Cluttering (Optional)[/u]
        CAP_Interior_Cluttering.ESP: Plugin file for cluttering the interior of the palace with plants.

[u]    03 Flame - Option 1 to 04 Flame - [u](Optional)[/u][/u]
        These folders contain different options for flames, each with its own set of mesh and texture files (where needed).
        Obviously you can choose only 1 type flame.
[u]
    04 Rotating Planets [u](Optional)[/u][/u]
        CAP_Rotating_Planets.ESP: Plugin file for adding rotating planets.

[u]    05 Doorstep - Vanilla hand and 05 Doorstep - ESO Style (Optional)[/u]
        These folders contain texture files for different doorstep styles.
[u]
    06 Columns - Dunmer Inscriptions (Columns) and  Columns - Dunmer Inscriptions (Palace) and Columns - Untouched Palace and others (Optionals)[/u]
        These folders contain texture and mesh files for different engraving options for the palace columns and palace itself.
        You should choose the right one for the type of palace of you choice. (Symmetrical, Asymmetrical, etc...)
        The Dunmer Letters Columns and Palace can be used together on the Symmetrical and Asymmetrical version.
               
[u]    07 Decorated Bridge (Optional)[/u]
        CAP_Bridge.ESP: Plugin file for decorating the bridge.

[u]    08 Cluttered Staircase [u](Optional)[/u][/u]
    CAP_Cluttered Staircase.ESP and CAP_Illuminated Staircase.ESP: Plugin files for cluttering and illuminating the staircase.
    You can use the CAP_Cluttered Staircase.ESP and CAP_Illuminated Staircase.ESP together.
     Contains a BcoM patch for the illuminated staircase.

[u]    09 Unique Door (Optional)[/u]
    CAP_Door.ESP: Plugin file for adding a unique door in the Vivec palace main entrance.

[u]    10 TR Water - Symmetric - Original Colour and others (Optional)[/u]
    These folders contain mesh files for different versions of water replacement. Use the symmetric version for the symmetric palace.
    Use the asymmetric version for the asymmetric palace etc. They come in different colors.

[u]    11 Vanilla Resolution Textures (Optional)[/u]
    Contains texture files for vanilla resolution textures.

As optional download you will find an OPENMW add on to see the dome flames (options 1 and 2) from afar. (Thanks to HeilKitty for this one)

[b]III. Compatibility:[/b]
This mod is compatible with any mod that does not directly alter Vivec's palace and bridge. Safe-to-use mods include Morrowind Rebirth, Dramatic Vivec, Versus Vivec, and Illuminated Palace of Vivec. Note that Distant Land currently cannot render animated objects, resulting in stationary planets and flameless domes from a distance.

[b]IV. Installation and Removal:
[/b]
To install, it's [u]highly recommended[/u] to use a mod manager such as Mod Organizer 2 or Wrye Mash, make your life easier.

If you want to do it manually, read carefully the folder descriptions above and follows the options for the various palaces as depicted in the last mod image.

In general:
If you choose the Symmetric version stick to symmetric options
If you chose the Asymmetric version stick  to Asymmetric options
If you choose the untouched palace stick to the untouched options.

While this mod should not harm your game, always create a backup as a precaution.

name: Better Flames for Concept Art Palace (Vivec City) - OpenMW Version
author: ChromedWolf
description: A simple texture modification for the green flames around Vivec Palace Dome
usage_notes:
The awesome [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48136]Concept Art Palace (Vivec City)[/url] mod creates a dramatic atmosphere for the whole Palace area, especially with the green flames that light up the nights.

The OpenMW version, though, for engine limitations doesn't (yet?) support the advanced glow and special effects, and only uses a flame texture on an animated mesh to achieve its result.

This mod is a very simple modification of the texture already provided by the OpenMWVersion of the C.A.P. original mod, improving its look and providing a better experience also to OpenMW players (well, it is of course subjective).

[size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size]

This is a simple texture edit, so you need the original mod to have everything work correctly:

From the original mod, you need to install

[list]
[*][b]00 Core[/b][/*]
[*][b]03 Flame - Option 2[/b] [i](you need the provided mesh to have this work correctly)[/i][/*]
[/list]
[i][u]You can of course select any other customization option from the original mod besides the flame!
[/u][/i]
Then you can install my own custom flame replacement. Inside my archive, you have two separate options:

[list]
[*][b]00 Green-Yellow[/b]: the original version, green-yellowish, looks closer to the original mod visuals[/*]
[*][b]00 Green-Blue[/b]: a new version added in v1.1.0, green-blueish, a color more similar to the windows on the palace dome and to the light orbs on the bridge.[/*]
[/list]
Pick only one, as they edit the same textures and are mutually exclusive. You can look at the screenshots for a comparison to make a choice (I recommend the green-blue version, as it has a more "magical fire" vibe than the original green-yellow "acid" look, but feel free to pick what you like the most) 

My modification should load AFTER the original mod, so make sure that the directories are in the correct order:

[code]﻿/path/to/openmw/data/concept-art-palace/00 Core
/path/to/openmw/data/concept-art-palace/03 Flame - Option 2
/path/to/openmw/data/better-flames/00 Green-Yellow (or /path/to/openmw/data/better-flames/00 Green-Blue)[/code] 

That's it, easy peasy.


[size=5][b]Credits[/b][/size]

A big thank to Vegetto88 and RandomPal for the original mods, of course all the credit goes to them.

name: Concept art Hlaalu Balconies
author: RandomPal -  Wolli  -  R0
description: Adds concept art balconies to the game, in Balmora and Suran.
usage_notes:
[size=3]I was looking at some Morrowind's conept art when I stumbled upon this drawing.[/size]

[img]https://images.uesp.net/4/44/MW-concept-19.jpg[/img]﻿

[size=3]One detail that really cought my eye was the balcony/staircase model. I was surprised to discovered that there wasn't a single mod that tried to implement that type of model into the game.

[b]As of version 2.0 the model has been remade from scratch[/b] by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/users/1615721]Wolli[/url]﻿, one of the best and most prolific modders and asset creators in the MW community.
There aren't many instances in the game where these new balconies can be used and I tried to use them well. Not every balcony has been replaced because variety is also improtant and because the vanilla balcony models are actually really good and I'd say iconic at this point.
The mod [b]also includes simple scenic balconies[/b] as seen in concept art. I used the models provided [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/43729]here[/url]. 
Due to the way vanilla design philosophy works, there wasn't a single place in the entire game where it made sense to use them, so it's not surprising that there ins't a mod making use of them. I expanded and tweaked 3 interior cells and replaced the exterior buildings with double floor versions to put these models to good use.
I hope you enjoy the mod!

[b]Installation[/b]
The mod is fully modular.
00 Core folder has the assets
01 adds the new balconies to Balmora
02 to Suran (with a version available for people using White Suran by MD)

[b]Compatibility
[/b]Should be compatible with pretty much everything. 
My mods [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48675]Suran - The Pearl of the Ascadian Island [/url]and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/48807]Balmora - Seat of Power of House Hlaalu[/url] already include the new balconies so you don't need this mod if you're using them.[/size]

name: Diverse Khajiit
author: Tiny Plesiosaur
description: All Khajiit on Vvardenfell in vanilla TES III are of the Suthay-Raht subtype. Diverse Khajiit is a simple mod that changes some Khajiit on Vvardenfell to be other subtypes of Khajiit from canon, using the variant Khajiit races from Tamriel_Data. (Also four Bretons become Reachmen or Riverfolk). Should be compatible with most everything, probably.
usage_notes:
[b]Diverse Khajiit will NOT work without Tamriel_Data installed. The AnimKit should no longer be necessary to see tails. Please comment if you still experience problems while using Tamriel_Data v26.08 (August 2026 release). [/b]I highly recommend using this mod alongside my other mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53710]All Races and Classes Enabled - Vanilla and Tamriel_Data[/url] so that you can also select the Khajiit subtypes as playable races.

Below is a full list of the NPCs edited by this mod. Besides their race, no part of these NPCs has been changed, aside from giving vanilla shoes to several of the newly plantigrade Khajiit. Faces/hairs are kept similar to vanilla when possible.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/100/images/48832/48832-1787730917-1362406942.png[/img]

New Khajiit types you may find:

[*][b]Cathay [/b]- Khajiit as seen in TES IV and TES V. They have tails, and can wear shoes. (NOTE - due to issues with the TD models, Cathay do not currently have tails. There is not a fix for this at this time.)[/*]
[*][b]Cathay-Raht [/b]- these are the largest bipedal Khajiit. They look like huge versions of the vanilla Khajiit. They have tails, and cannot wear shoes.[/*]
[*][b]Ohmes [/b]- Khajiit as seen in TES I. They look a lot like elves from a distance. They can wear shoes.[/*]
[*][b]Ohmes-Raht [/b]- Khajiit as seen in TES II. They look kind of like Ohmes, but a bit fuzzier. Ohmes-Raht have tails and can wear shoes.[/*]
[*][b]Suthay [/b]- Small Khajiit who look a bit like smaller versions of the vanilla Khajiit, right down to the heads and tails, but they can wear shoes.[/*]
[*][b]Dagi-Raht[/b] - ﻿[b]New in October 2023 version![/b] These short-furred Khajiit have a very unique look, with wide eyes and almost skeletal figures. They have tails and cannot wear shoes.[/*]
[*][b]Tojay - New in August 2026 version! [/b]These thick-furred Khajiit resemble Manul cats. They can wear shoes but often do not.[/*]
[*]Additionally, two NPCs in Vvardenfell with already-fitting names  are now [b]Reachmen[/b], the people of the stormy borderlands between Skyrim, High Rock, and Hammerfell.[/*]
[*]Two other Bretons  with appropriate vanilla names are now Riverfolk, the people of the Bjoulsae Basin between High Rock and Hammerfell.[/*]
[*]As another added bonus, some nameless Khajiit Quarra vampires are now spooky vampiric Dagi-Rahts. These will give you a fright!

[b]This mod does not break Khajiit-style dialogue! All Khajiit should talk in the usual Khajiit speech patterns.[/b]

name: Sotha Sil is a Dunmer
author: G The Generous
description: A slight tweak for Sotha Sil's texture so that he is no longer an n'wah
usage_notes:
[b]New 2.0 version revamped HD version using Sotha Sil texture from Intelligent Textures 2.1, vanilla version remains the same. Special thanks to Remiros for it![/b]

[b]Description:[/b]
Sotha Sil is the saddest god in the whole TES universe, not only that you can't *ahem* interact with him, Bethesda also didn't even give him a proper unique face, they just took the face texture of corprus stalker then slapped on his already sad and miserable face. And then years later, even though we have mods that make Vivec and Almalexia look like Kim Kardashian and the like, no one still bother to give poor old Sotha some love.

Sotha Sil is a Dunmer is a simple edit to his texture, it mostly remains the same but Sotha Sil's skin is now Dunmer-like with the iconic red eyes, I
also changed the shape of his eyebrows so it looks more elven. I'm not very excellent at texture editing, it's not much but I figured it's better than his abomination vanilla face. This is initially an optional file for my HD Vanilla Textures but as there are now better upscaled textures out there, I think it deserves its own place and I also used a better upscaled texture as a base and reworking it from there.

There are 2 versions: HD and Vanilla, both are in the same file. HD version is for people who use Intelligent Textures or other texture packs, Vanilla version is for vanilla purists because PURITY!!!

Kartoffels for Sotha Sil base texture used for version 1
Remiros for Sotha Sil base texture from IT 2.1

Orange Narsis uses the unatlased vanilla meshes as its base, I just swapped them for their Project Atlas equivalents and made two new atlas textures for them using MET.

The Velothi parts are not an exact 1 to 1 recreation but shouldn't be too noticeably different; the flat part of the temple roof around the dome uses the darker wall texture rather than the patina copper so is more similar to the vanilla design, and the same is true of the tower door.

description: Reduces the size of the blight cloud inside the crater of Red Mountain to improve compatibility with shaders.
usage_notes:

name: S3maphore - Music That Moves With the World
author: S3ctorOMW
description: The open-ended music system OpenMW was supposed to have. Fast, flexible playlists that react to every place, fight, faction, and feeling.
usage_notes:
[center][size=6][b][color=#b48cff]S3MAPHORE[/color][/b][/size]
[size=4][i]Your music. Your rules.[/i][/size]

[b][i]Brought to You by DreamWeave-MP[/i][/b][/center]

[center][size=4][b]Modern, contextual music management for OpenMW.[/b][/size]

No compromises. No bullshit. Your music responds to the world around you.[/center]

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]REQUIREMENTS[/color][/center]
[/heading]

[list]
[*][b]OpenMW 0.51 or newer[/b] — [url=https://openmw.org/downloads]Download OpenMW[/url][/*]
[*][b]H3lp Yours3lf[/b] — [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56417]Download H3lp Yours3lf[/url][/*]
[/list]
[heading][center][color=#b48cff]START HERE — WHAT ARE YOU TRYING TO DO?[/color][/center]
[/heading]

[color=#b48cff][b][size=5]I just want S3maphore to manage normal Morrowind music.[/size][/b][/color]

Install S3maphore, enable [font=Courier New]00 Core[/font], and enable [font=Courier New]S3maphore.esp[/font].

[b]You're done.[/b]

Vanilla Explore and Battle music should work immediately.

[color=#b48cff][b][size=5]I installed a music mod that S3maphore supports.[/size][/b][/color]

Install the music mod normally, then enable the matching S3maphore playlist module.

For example, MUSE-style music packs use [font=Courier New]03 Muse Expansion Playlists[/font].

[b]You do not need to edit the music mod or S3maphore's Lua files.[/b]

[color=#b48cff][b][size=5]I want to add my own music.[/size][/b][/color]

[center][b][color=#ffcc66][size=6]PUT THE AUDIO FILES IN THE PLAYLIST'S MUSIC FOLDER.[/size][/color][/b]
[b]There is [color=#b48cff]no Lua step[/color].
There is [color=#b48cff]no filename-registration step[/color].
There is [color=#b48cff]no [i]S3maphore[/i] configuration file[/color] you need to edit.[/b][/center]

S3maphore's playlist modules already contain the rules deciding [i]when[/i] music should play. You supply the music by placing supported audio files in the folder that playlist reads.

The empty [font=Courier New]Music[/font] directories included with S3maphore are intentional drop zones.

The [font=Courier New].gitkeep[/font] files inside them are only placeholders used to preserve empty directories. Ignore them.

For example:

[code]03 Muse Expansion Playlists/
└── Music/
    └── ms/
        └── cell/
            └── hlaalu/
                ├── my-hlaalu-track.mp3
                └── another-track.mp3[/code]
Those tracks are now available to the existing Hlaalu playlist.

[b]You may also provide the same [font=Courier New]Music/...[/font] path from another enabled OpenMW data directory.[/b] The files do not have to be copied directly into S3maphore.

See [b][color=#b48cff][size=4]WHERE TO PUT YOUR MUSIC[/size][/color][/b] below for every existing playlist folder.

[color=#b48cff][size=4][b]I want music to play somewhere S3maphore does not already have a playlist for.[/b][/size][/color]

That is when playlist authoring becomes relevant.

Creating entirely new contextual behavior uses S3maphore's Lua playlist API and is intended for mod authors.

[url=https://dreamweave-mp.github.io/S3ctors-S3cret-St4sh/s3maphore/docs/][b][color=#b48cff]Playlist Author Documentation[/color][/b][/url]

[center][color=#d4d4d8][b]If you are only installing S3maphore, installing supported music packs, or adding songs to existing playlists, you do not need to open or edit a .lua file.[/b][/color][/center]

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]INSTALLATION[/color][/center]
[/heading]
[center][size=5][b][color=#ffcc66]Enable 00 Core and S3maphore.esp.[/color][/b][/size]
[b]Everything else in the S3maphore archive is optional.[/b][/center]

[size=4][b]Using an OpenMW mod manager[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]1.[/b] Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/56417]H3lp Yours3lf[/url].[/*]
[*][b]2.[/b] Install S3maphore.[/*]
[*][b]3.[/b] Enable the [font=Courier New]00 Core[/font] data directory.[/*]
[*][b]4.[/b] Enable [font=Courier New]S3maphore.esp[/font] in OpenMW's content list.[/*]
[*][b]5.[/b] Enable only optional modules matching music or content you actually use.[/*]
[*][b]6.[/b] Launch the game.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Installation test:[/b] if normal Explore and Battle music plays, S3maphore Core is installed correctly.

[color=#ffcc66][b]Do not enable every module blindly.[/b][/color]

Optional modules define additional playlists. Many expect music supplied by another mod or by you. If S3maphore cannot find any tracks belonging to one of those playlists, it simply leaves that playlist inactive.

[size=4][b]Manual OpenMW installation[/b][/size]

S3maphore is packaged as several separate OpenMW data directories.

[b]Do not flatten them into Morrowind's [font=Courier New]Data Files[/font] directory.[/b]

Add only the directories you want to [font=Courier New]openmw.cfg[/font].

For example:

[code]data="/path/to/S3maphore/00 Core"
data="/path/to/S3maphore/03 Muse Expansion Playlists"[/code]
Then enable [font=Courier New]S3maphore.esp[/font] from [font=Courier New]00 Core[/font].

[color=#d4d4d8][b]Important:[/b] module numbers are labels, not load-order requirements. They do not need to be enabled in numerical order.[/color]

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]WHERE TO PUT YOUR MUSIC[/color][/center]
[/heading]

[center][size=4][b]Adding your own tracks? This is the section you want.[/b][/size]

Choose the existing playlist you want to supply music for and put your audio files in its listed [font=Courier New]Music/...[/font] folder.

[b]For folder-based playlists, every supported audio file in that folder is discovered automatically. Do not add its filename to a Lua file.[/b]

[b]Use the documented folder names [color=#b48cff]exactly[/color]. Do not [color=#b48cff]invent, rename, or reorganize[/color] them.[/b]
[/center]

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]WHAT S3MAPHORE DOES[/color][/center]
[/heading]

S3maphore replaces OpenMW's built-in music handling with contextual playlists.

Music can react to location, region, cell, faction, enemy, weather, time, tileset, magic effects, or damn near anything else OpenMW exposes to Lua.

For normal users, that complexity is already handled by the installed playlist modules.

You provide music. S3maphore decides when it plays.

For mod authors, the underlying model is:

[list]
[*][b]Playlist[/b] — a collection of tracks with rules for when it may play.[/*]
[*][b]Priority[/b] — decides which valid playlist wins.[/*]
[*][b]Playdeck[/b] — every playlist S3maphore discovers in your OpenMW installation.[/*]
[/list]
When game state changes, S3maphore checks the playdeck and [b]deals[/b] the highest-priority valid playlist.

Battle music is not magic. It is simply a playlist with a combat condition and high priority.

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]MUSE-STYLE MUSIC PACKS[/color][/center]
[/heading]

S3maphore supports music packs and folder conventions originally designed for MUSE. MUSE itself is an MWSE mod and does not run in OpenMW; you [color=#b48cff]do not need MUSE[/color].

[font=Courier New]03 Muse Expansion Playlists[/font] contains playlist definitions. It does [b]not[/b] include the original music packs.

Install the music pack first, then enable [font=Courier New]03 Muse Expansion Playlists[/font].

[color=#d4d4d8][b]General rule:[/b] if S3maphore finds no tracks for a playlist, it ignores that playlist. Missing music does not fill your game with errors.[/color]

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]COMPATIBILITY[/color][/center]
[/heading]

Music mods that add or replace tracks in [font=Courier New]Music/Explore[/font], [font=Courier New]Music/Battle[/font], or [font=Courier New]Music/Special[/font] work with S3maphore automatically.

Playlist-based music packs are different. Their tracks may live in custom folders, so S3maphore needs matching playlist definitions.

The included compatibility modules provide those definitions for supported MUSE-style packs, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/53568]Dynamic Music[/url] soundbanks, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51734]Morrow Winds[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/morrowind/mods/51769]CaptainCreepy Music Pack[/url], and other music mods.

S3maphore compatibility modules replace the playlist/controller logic required by supported Lua- or MWSE-based music systems. Install the music files they provide, but do not expect their original scripting systems to function under OpenMW.

Mods that play music directly through MWScript are separate. S3maphore does not replace or disable that interface.

[heading][center][color=#b48cff]TROUBLESHOOTING[/color][/center]
[/heading]

[center][size=4][b]If you edited any S3maphore .lua files while trying to add music, restore or reinstall S3maphore before troubleshooting.

Adding music [color=#b48cff]DOES NOT[/color] require Lua changes.[/b][/size][/center]

[size=4][b]No music plays at all[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]1.[/b] Confirm that [font=Courier New]00 Core[/font] is enabled.[/*]
[*][b]2.[/b] Confirm that [font=Courier New]S3maphore.esp[/font] is enabled in OpenMW's content list.[/*]
[*][b]3.[/b] Confirm that H3lp Yours3lf is installed.[/*]
[*][b]4.[/b] Confirm that S3maphore's numbered directories were not flattened into [font=Courier New]Data Files[/font].[/*]
[/list]
If vanilla Explore and Battle music works, [font=Courier New]00 Core[/font] is installed correctly.

[size=4][b]Vanilla music works, but an optional playlist does not[/b][/size]

Confirm that:

[list]
[*]The matching S3maphore module is enabled.[/*]
[*]The music pack it expects is installed.[/*]
[*]The expected tracks exist somewhere in OpenMW's virtual file system.[/*]
[/list]
If S3maphore finds no tracks for a playlist, that playlist stays inactive.

[size=4][b]Still nothing? Time to interrogate the log.[/b][/size]

Enable S3maphore debug messages and inspect [font=Courier New]openmw.log[/font].

S3maphore messages begin with:

[code][ S3MAPHORE ][/code]
[heading][center][color=#b48cff]FOR PLAYLIST AUTHORS[/color][/center]
[/heading]

S3maphore playlists are Lua modules.

Use built-in rules or combine them into entirely new conditions. The public documentation covers playlist creation, priorities, rules, events, metadata, and the S3maphore interface.
